On the preceding day, having made the *stotrīya* verse correspond to that of the following day, he recites it. (Section 5) 24.
Thus ends the second chapter of the sixteenth book in the *Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-Sūtra*.

"Anurūpa" means similar. This is established by logic due to the statement, "There are no lineages lacking [in excellence]. Thus ends the second chapter of the sixteenth book in the *Prayogacandrikā*, a commentary on the *Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-Sūtra* compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī.
Now begins the third chapter of the sixteenth book.
During the Atirātra sacrifice, he assigns the milk products.

Āpastamba states: "While the Atirātra is still in progress, he assigns the milks for the following day. While the Atirātra is still in progress, once the *ṣoḍaśin* cups have been washed, he assigns the milks for the following day with the formulas beginning, "That which is the milk-yielding cow for the sacrificer's vow," and so forth. The procedures for milking and so on have already been explained. 1.

When the Maitrāvaruṇa announces, "Tomorrow is the Soma-pressing; announce the Soma to Indra and Agni, to the All-gods, and to the Soma-drinking Brāhmaṇas," the Āgnīdhra enters his own chamber and issues the command: "Tomorrow is the Soma-pressing; I announce the Soma to Indra and Agni, to the All-gods, and to the Soma-drinking Brāhmaṇas; O Brahman, restrain your speech; O Subrahmaṇya, invoke the Subrahmaṇyā. || 2 ||

When the Hāriyojana cup has been offered on the day of the Aharaha-gava-vimokṣa, [the Adhvaryu] announces, "The Soma-pressing is tomorrow. Then the Āgnīdhra, having entered the Āgnīdhra shed, issues the command: "The Soma-pressing is tomorrow."
362: — *Śrautasūtra* composed by Satyāṣāḍha—In the sixteenth book:
"On this day, one should say 'today is the Soma-pressing,' or [one should say] 'the Soma-pressing is tomorrow' on other days. (3)

‘“He should indeed say, ‘The Soma-pressing is tomorrow,’ says Āśmarathya; ‘The Soma-pressing is today,’ says Ālekhana,” so says Āpastamba. Therefore, [the rule] “The Soma-pressing is tomorrow” is not subject to numerical limitation here. ||3||
The day concludes with the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings. || 4 ||
The ritual action is completed with the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings. || 4 ||
When he has passed away, Brahmā releases his speech. || 5 ||
When the day has concluded, at the end of the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings, the Brahman priest releases his speech.
They pour out water for the wives. || 6 ||
At one time, they set aside water for their wives for the purpose of drinking; such is the meaning. || 6 ||
Those who carry the fuel-bundles take them away. ||7||
The sacrificers' men [perform] the fetching of the fuel-sticks. || 7 ||
Having returned, they place fuel-sticks upon the Āhavanīya fire.
Having returned, they take these fuel-sticks and place them upon the Āhavanīya fire.
In this manner, they should be performed day after day.
He has gone. ||9||
On that day, there is the Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha.

Then follows the carrying around of the *vasatīvarī* waters to the northern fire-altar; the consecration of the *sannā* grass; the cutting of the branch for the *savanīya* offering; and the fetching of the fuel and sacrificial grass (*idhmābarhis*), and so forth. On both sides, the drawing of the *vasatīvarī* waters takes place on the preceding day itself. If even one of these acts is omitted, an oblation is offered with the mantra: "Homage to Brahman. (10)
The Agniṣṭoma sacrifice is threefold and has the Rathantara as its Sāman.

This is the specific distinction regarding the *upayaj* offerings. At the time of employing the Soma-vessels, the vessel for the *atigrāhya* cup dedicated to Agni is indeed used first for three days, according to the injunction. At the time of the *ṛtukaraṇa*, there is no oblation; rather, after reciting the *yajus*, there is the heating of the vessels for Indra and Vāyu. At the time of the animal sacrifice, one dedicates a ewe to Sarasvatī following the *trivṛt* [stomas]. The mention of the *upaśaya* lying to the north of the *agniṣṭha* post is not an injunction. As before, they should perform this at the time of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). || 11 ||
With the sound of the chariot, he introduces the hymn for Mahendra. || 12 ||
In the Nyāyasūtra, this sūtra is for the purpose of a technical definition (*paribhāṣā*) because it provides an explanation for another sūtra; the same applies in the case of Āpastamba. 12.
The sound of the *upākaraṇa* mantra is a modification.

At the time of commencing the Māhendra-stotra, the commencement of the Māhendra-stotra is performed with the sound of a cart; the sound [of the cart] takes the place of the mantra. Even then, one maintains [the ritual] as before. While the Yajñāyajñīya is being chanted, he draws the Vasatīvarī waters. In the daily-performance (pratidina) option, there is no throwing away of the antelope horn; it concludes with the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings and the placing of the fuel-sticks (samid-ādhāna), as before. 13.
The Ukthya sacrifice with fifteen stomas has the Bṛhat Sāman.

"Tomorrow is the *sutyā*," and so forth. During the night, the ritual procedure (*tantra*) begins with the carrying away of the *vasatīvarī* waters and ends with the strewing of grass (*paristaraṇa*). When dawn has broken at the great hour (*mahārātre*), having awakened, there is the *pañcadaśa-ukthya* sacrifice with the *bṛhat-sāman*. At the time of placing the Soma vessels, according to the Vājasaneya tradition, only the *aindrātigrāhya* vessel is used as before. There is the bringing forward of the Soma; "I yoke Agni. In the daily-offering version, there is only one *atigrāhya*, the *śukra-āmaya*, which is dedicated to Indra.

At the time for the animal sacrifice, the victim is a sheep (*saunya*); by way of transposition, it is placed on the southern sacrificial post (*yūpa*), with the instruction that it lies near the fire-post (*agniṣṭha*). || 14 ||
With the sound of a drum, he begins the hymn of praise dedicated to Mahendra. || 15 ||
At the time of commencing the Māhendra hymn, the meaning is that the commencement of the hymn takes place with the sound of the drum (dundubhi)—that is, the well-known muraja drum. || 15 ||
If there is thunder, that very sound shall be the modification of the mantra for the introductory rite (upākaraṇa). || 16 ||

Or, as before, with the sound of thunder. At the time of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), from the *yajñāyajñīya* chant through the *vasatīvarī* waters up to the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings, and the placing of the fuel-sticks (*samidādhāna*) are as before. The continuity of the *ahīna* sacrifice lasts until the spreading of the grass at night.
The Ukthya sacrifice consists of seventeen [stotras] and has the Vairūpa as its sāman.

On the following day, O Great King, having understood [the ritual], there is the seventeen-fold Ukthya sacrifice with the Vairūpa Sāman. At the time of setting out the vessels, there is only one vessel for the Saura Atigrāhya cup. The performance of the seasonal rites (*ṛtukaraṇa*) is like that of the Ukthya. During the Āgrayaṇa drawing, the Saura Atigrāhya is drawn from the Āgrayaṇa vessel. At the time of the animal sacrifice, having encircled [the post] with a triple-twisted cord, a dark-colored animal dedicated to Pūṣan is designated as lying near the northern sacrificial post of the Agniṣṭha. || 17 ||
With the *ādhāva* verse, he introduces the *māhendra* hymn of praise. || 18 ||
At that time, there is running about. || 18 ||
The *barhis* grass is a modification; when that has been brought forward and the *prastāva* has been chanted, the Udgātṛ shakes himself with a spray of water. || 19 ||

At the time of commencing the *māhendra* stotra, he shakes [the vessel] with the *āghāra* offering while standing outside; thus he performs the commencement of the stotra. When the *prastāva* has been chanted, the Udgātṛ shakes [it] with the *āghāra* offering. At the time of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), he gives [it] as before. At the time of the *yajñāyajñīya* chant, from the pouring of the *vasatīvarī* waters up to the placing of the fuel-sticks, it is as before: the continuity of the *ahīna* sacrifice up to the strewing of the grass-bundle (*paristaraṇa*). || 19 ||
The twenty-first [stotra] is the Ṣoḍaśī, having the Vairāja as its sāman. || 16.3.20 ||

The Great King, having understood that on the following day they will perform the twenty-first *ṣoḍaśin* sacrifice with the *vairāja-sāman*, [this is] the remainder [of the instruction]. Alternatively, as in the case of the *ukthya*, the *ṣoḍaśin* is not [performed] in the intervals, because of the statement "that is the *ukthya*. Here, if there is a *ṣoḍaśin*, then in the first three-day period, one takes exactly three *atigrāhya* cups; in the second three-day period, from today onwards, one takes the *atigrāhya* cup dedicated to Agni.
[Satyāṣāḍha-viracitaṃ Śrautasūtram—16th Praśna]

The sequence begins with the cup for Indra and Vāyu. At the time of the animal sacrifice, there is a white-backed animal dedicated to Bṛhaspati; it is designated as lying near the southern post of the Agniṣṭha fire. 20.
There is a *nyūṅkha* [insertion of the syllable 'hum'] at the calls of *haviṣkṛt*, *āśruta*, and *pratyāśruta*, and he performs the *nyūṅkha* at the *pratigara*. || 21 ||

On this day, there are *nyūṅkhas*. The *adhikāra* and so forth, such as "nyūṅkha," "o," "o," and so on, pertain to the office of the *hotṛ*. This has been explained at length by the venerable Āśvalāyana in the passage beginning with "on the fourth day, the opening verse of the *prātaranuvāka*," and so forth. The response (*pratigara*) follows precisely the path prescribed for each respective occasion. 21.
With the two kindling woods he introduces the hymn to Mahendra; this is a modification of the sacrificial grass.

As before, he gives [the dakṣiṇā] at the time of the sacrificial fee. At the time of the commencement of the Māhendra-stotra, two fire-drills and a pair of darbha-grass blades have been brought forward in place of the sacrificial grass (barhis). || 22 ||

When that [animal] has been brought near and presented, (Khaṇḍa 6) ||23|| the Udgātṛ, having covered his right thigh with Avakā plants and placed the two fire-drills thereon, churns the fire. ||24|| Once it has been produced, the Udgātṛ, having uttered the *abhihiṅkāra*, hands it to the Prastotṛ. ||25|| The Prastotṛ [hands it] to the Adhvaryu. ||26||

When the *sāman* has been introduced and the *stomabhāga* verses have been recited, the Udgātṛ then presses down upon his right thigh with his heel, places two pieces of fire-drill wood (*araṇī*) upon it, and produces fire by friction. When that fire has been produced, the Adhvaryu and Pratiprasthātṛ [take it]; the Udgātṛ, having uttered the *hiṃ* over it, utters the *hiṃ* again over it. The Udgātṛ then hands it to the Prastotṛ. || 23 || 24 || 25 || 26 ||

Having carried it around the hearths with the front [of the ladle] and having thrown it into the Āhavanīya fire, he makes an offering over it with the Virāj verse: "O Agni, being kindled, shine forth. || 27 ||

The Prastotṛ hands it to the Adhvaryu; the Adhvaryu, having carried it around the north of the Dhiṣṇiya hearths, places it on the northern side of the Āgnīdhra hearth itself, and then casts it into the Āhavanīya fire with the Virāj verse, "Preddho agne" (O Agni, shine forth). The rest is as explained previously. || 27 ||
The Ukthya sacrifice has twenty-seven verses; its Sāman is the Śākvara.

Some [say]: from the time of the *yajñāyajñīya* chant until the end of the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings, and ending with the placing of the fuel-sticks (*samidādhāna*), it is as before. The continuity of the *ahīna* sacrifice is as before, up to the spreading of the sacrificial grass (*paristaraṇa*). On the following day at dawn, having understood [the procedure], they enter upon the *triṇava-ukthya* sacrifice characterized by the *śākvara-sāman*; this is the remainder [of the instruction]. The *mahānāmnī* verses are the *pṛṣṭha* chant, but there are no *ātagrāhya* cups. As before, in the case of the three-day (*tryaha*) option, there is one cup for Indra and one for Śukra. At the time of the animal sacrifice, the *śilpa* cup belongs to Viśve Devāḥ. From the *agniṣṭha* post onwards, on the fourth [day] to the north, there is the indication of the resting place (*upaśaya*), as before, at the time of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). 28.

With waters that have been sprinkled over with barley-grains, he introduces the *stotra* for Mahendra. When that [introductory rite] has been performed, there is a modification of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) once the *prastāva* has been chanted. || 29 ||

Āpastamba states: "At the time of commencing the *stotra* for the *māhendra* cup, the commencement of the *stotra* takes place with waters containing *avakā* plants—those *avakā* plants which were thrown into the waters in place of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*)—and the *sāman* is commenced once the two blades of grass have been laid down" (ĀpŚS 21.7.10).
Three cows with bulls go ahead along the northern path from the *sadas* to the *āgnīdhra*, crossing by way of the southern path.

Three bulls, three cows, and one ox are led northward in front of the *sadas* and behind the *āgnīdhra*. In an *ahīna* sacrifice, the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*) for the officiating priests are given along the southern path; however, in a *sattra*, there is no giving, nor do the ritual duties pertaining to the *dakṣiṇā* apply. From the *patnīsaṃyāja* onwards, up to the placing of the *samidh* sticks, the continuity of the *ahīna* rites is maintained, ending with the spreading of the *paristaraṇa* grass.
The Ukthya sacrifice with the Raivata Sāman is for the Thirty-three [gods]. ||31||

The word "they undertake" (*upayanti*) is to be supplied as the remainder of the sentence. On the next day at the great pressing, having performed the *ukthya* sacrifice with thirty-three stotras and the *Raivata* as its *sāman*, they undertake [the rite], but there are no *atigrāhya* cups. As before, whether in the case of the first three-day period (*tryaha*) or the subsequent three-day period, one employs only a single *atigrāhya* cup dedicated to Sūrya. As before, in the case of the first three-day period and the two following ones, there are no *atigrāhya* cups. According to some, one takes all [the cups] at the first [pressing]. Because it is an *āgniṣṭoma*, [the draught] is from the *āgrayaṇa* vessel. At the time for the animal sacrifice, [the victim] is dedicated to Indra; [he says]: "I dedicate thee, acceptable to Indra. To the south, the fourth [victim] is designated as lying down, as before. || 31 ||
This day consists of the *nyūṅkha* interjection;
the response (*pratigara*) follows accordingly.
The Ṛtuyāja is performed by himself. || 33 ||
"The householder himself [should perform the rites]," says Āpastamba (ĀpaŚrSū 21.7.14). || 33 ||
When it is said, "O two Adhvaryus, sacrifice," the Adhvaryu, having entered the two Havirdhāna sheds, sacrifices either with the subsequent ṛc or with the subsequent *praiṣa* (direction). || 34 ||

The Adhvaryu himself performs the Ṛtuyājana offering. Having recognized [the signal], he says, "O Gṛhapati, sacrifice! Then the Adhvaryu, having entered the Havirdhāna shed, issues the call for the two subsequent offerings. The rest is clear. || 34 ||

"O Aśvins, drink the pressed [Soma] (the honey), you who shine with fire and possess pure vows, you who are the bearers of the sacrifice according to the season! By the season, drink the Soma—Vauṣaṭ! Thus he sacrifices even when the [verse] is not expanded; [he sacrifices with "drink" when it is not expanded]. ||35||
He utters "vauṣaṭ" as the *vaṣaṭ* call; likewise for the householder, if [the fire] has been carried forward. || 35 ||

16. Regarding the *Vyūḍhacaturhotṛ*: "O you two who carry men, yoke today this chariot facing hither; here is your unyoking. Mix the oblations with honey, for indeed, you have arrived; then drink the Soma, O you who possess wealth in horses! Drink the Soma according to the season, *vauṣaṭ*! Thus, its performance proceeds with the *Marutvatīya* offerings (the word "drink" is used when the *caturhotṛ* is in the *vyūḍha* form). || 36 ||

When the [Soma] has been carried forward on the day of the Upavasatha, at the time of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the ritual procedure for that which has been offered proceeds with the Marutvatīya cups. || 36 ||
When that which is prior to the Mahendra cup has been performed, the Pratiprasthātṛ, having stretched the cord toward the north behind the Āgnīdhra fire-shed, binds the calves to it.

The Māhendra cup has not been consumed; the Marutvatīya cup has been consumed. Here the Pratiprasthātṛ performs the rite: having spread out and extended the line of calves toward the north outside the Āgnīdhra shed, he drives the calves along that line. || 37 ||
To the south of the Mārjālīya fire, they confine the mothers. || 38 ||
The name [of this rite] is Mantivatsāmnām.
|| 38 || At the place of the *barhis* grass, he begins the *Māhendra* hymn with water and *dūrvā* grass spread out; it is a modification of the *barhis*. || 39 ||

They remain there, either bound or unbound. Then the Māhendra [cup] is drawn with waters standing on the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), or rather with those waters in which *dūrvā* grass has been cast; this is for the purpose of commencing the chant (*stotropa-karaṇa*). || 39 ||

When that [rite] has been initiated and commenced, having released the calves from their mothers and having led them along the southern path of its northern direction, they settle down; thus concludes the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha. (kha07) || 16.3.40 ||
Thus ends the third chapter in the sixteenth book of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi Sūtra.

With those [cows], the commencement of the chant (*stotropa-karaṇa*) and the preparation of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) have been performed, and the Sāman has not yet been chanted. Then, having reunited these calves with their mothers, they perform the *sāṃkāśina* rite to the north of the *āsīdha*. The attendants of the cows and the calves lead them quickly; that is, they drive them along the south side of the *sadah* and the *āsīdha* pavilion toward the north. However, in a *sattra* sacrifice, there is no giving because it is prohibited; whereas in an *ahīna* sacrifice, he gives to the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*).

As before, [the ritual proceeds] until the *patnīsaṃyāja* at the time of the *yajñāyajñīya* chant. In the case of the *samīpa* arrangement, the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* concludes with five [days]. Thus ends the third chapter in the sixteenth book of the *Prayogacandrikā*, compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī, which is an exposition of the *Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-sūtra*.
5: Paṭala Five] Accompanied by the commentary *Prayogacandrikā* compiled by Mahādeva Śākhin. 16.4 Now begins the fourth paṭala in the sixteenth praśna.
When the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* has been completed, they consume either clarified butter or honey. || 1 ||
Every day there are three Ukthya days, and [then] the Chandomas. ||2||

When the next day has dawned, having understood that the tenth day is the *avivākya*, they perform the twenty-four-fold *agniṣṭoma*. The group for the *prāyaṇīya* and *udayanīya* rites is stated as beginning with "O Agni, lead us...

The [stomas] are the twenty-four-fold, the forty-four-fold, and the forty-eight-fold; the twenty-four-fold is the *avivākya*. The tenth day is an *agniṣṭoma* Soma sacrifice with the *rathantara* as its *sāman*. (3)
"The tenth day" means on the tenth day within this [period]. || 3 ||
In this, nothing whatsoever is obstructed for anyone. || 4 ||

If anyone at all should strike one who is afflicted, destroyed, or fallen from his status, one should not explain it to him, thinking: "This has been destroyed by you; this is the expiation. This is the sense.
(4) If those outsiders who are mere observers should speak there, they would find nothing within; thus, the good and the evil are declared. (5)

Those outsiders who are spectators outside the assembly hall, those spectators, shall depart as onlookers. It should be understood that this [act] has been destroyed by you; this is the expiation. || 5 ||
If they should not find [the required items] there, they should be announced by the householder.

If they should not know [the details] therein, the householder, being addressed, must explain that there is a single expiation for a ruined object, with the sense: "This has been destroyed; this is the expiation for this. || 6 ||
Having recited the Gṛhapati hymn in the Anuṣṭubh meter, he should say that [verse].
At the time of speaking, having recited a verse in the *anuṣṭubh* meter, this expiation is performed for what has been ruined in this [rite]. || 7 ||
At which [verse] he pronounces the invitation, he should also accomplish the *ānuṣṭubh* meter together with that very [verse]. On that day, they bring two fuel-sticks. 8.
Whatever is to be said regarding one who is afflicted should be stated by means of a verse known as an *anuṣṭubh*. In that regard, the verse according to the method described is:
*ṭāḥ*—[from the Śrautasūtra composed by Satyāṣāḍha, Book 16].

O Adhvaryu, a reversal is prescribed in this case: having touched the *havirdhāna* (sacrificial cart) with the verse "O Agni, lead us," one should recite two verses. After reciting the *anuṣṭubh* verse, the expiation is stated by means of this *śloka*. The *śloka* prescribing the expiation is as follows: "O Agni, you are ours; and you are ours; Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ (Svastha), and likewise; the muttering (*japa*) of the *anājñāta* [mantras], and the supreme remembrance of Murāri."

Thus follows the rule for expiation, beginning with "O Agni, lead us," and so forth. There are three *atigrāhya* cups. When the *gaurīvita* Sāman is present, the drawing of the *atigrāhya* cups occurs on the tenth day; for there is a scriptural injunction stating that even in the *agniṣṭoma*, wherever the *gaurīvita* Sāman is used, one takes many *atigrāhya* cups. At the time of the silent pressing (*upāṃśu-abhiṣava*), the drawing of the *pṛśni-prāṇagraha* cups has already been described. [The cup] for Vāyu is this one. At the time of the animal sacrifice, there is a ram dedicated to Varuṇa. To the south, the instruction regarding the resting place for the horse is as previously stated.
At the time of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), as before, having performed the rites up to the Patnīsaṃyājas during the Yajñāyajñīya chant, they bring fuel-sticks according to the rule for this day.
And the *audumbarī* posts are permanent.
"Bringing fuel" is an elliptical reference [to a preceding rule]. || 9 ||
They place [the fuel] on continuously. 16.4.10.
The word "āhavanīya" is to be understood as the ellipsis. || 10 ||
To the north of the Āhavanīya fire, they place a post made of Udumbara wood.
The meaning is that they establish [it]. || 11 ||

With the two verses, "The sunless ones near the sun," and "Those with which the sun [travels]," he offers oblations into the Gārhapatya fire: "These [rays] speed our sacrifice here; here is delight, here is pleasure; rejoice here! Here is pleasure, here is delight; rejoice here! Your delight is here. He offers with these two verses into the Gārhapatya fire. 12.
When they have been touched together, he makes two offerings on the Gārhapatya fire with two verses. || 12 ||

"This thousand-rayed one is the vision of the poets; the mind, possessing the nature of light, has sustained them. With this *aticchandas* verse, "He has set the dawns in harmony—spotless, dwelling together, of equal seed, and of one mind; even those who possess voice and fury have come to him," they worship the Āhavanīya fire. (Section 8) 13.

Then, having gone to the Āhavanīya fire, they worship it with the *aticchandas* verse, "Ayaṃ sahasramānavaḥ," which is sung in a melodic chant (*pragīta*); so say the Mīmāṃsakas. It is understood that this is the statement of the Sūtrakāra regarding the Chāndogas. || 13 ||
They proceed toward the Prājāpatya cup for the seizing of the mind. || 14 ||
Then the Brahman, the Adhvaryu, and the Udgātṛ proceed toward the Pājāpatya Manograha.
[Chapter 4] Accompanied by the *Prayogacandrikā* commentary compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrin, page 369:

When [the Soma] has flowed forth, while meditating on the earth with his mind, he draws the cup for Prajāpati with the formula: "With this vessel, I take thee, acceptable to Prajāpati Manu"—thus he draws the *manograha* (mind-cup) for Prajāpati. From the space [of the sky], or from the Soma remaining after the third pressing, he should cause it to be cooked until it is sufficient for one group of *camasa*-cups.

"When [the Soma] has flowed forth, he draws [the cup] silently with the Upāṃśu vessel"—this is the injunction. With the formula, "By this [vessel], I draw thee, acceptable to Prajāpati," he draws it after meditating on Ākāśa according to its form. Or, having meditated on a portion of Ākāśa, he draws it at the time of bringing up the Agniṣṭoma cups for one group of cups. It is as much as is obtained, that is, limited. || 15 ||
Therefore, he should draw [the cup] with the Upāṃśu vessel; he pours out the cups, of which the Hotṛ’s cup is the first. There are both a Stotra and a Śastra.
He has gone. || 16 || 17 ||

Everything for him is performed mentally. (18) He introduces the hymn of praise mentally. (19) He chants the *prastāva* mentally. (20) He chants the *udgītha* mentally. (21) He chants the *pratihāra* mentally. (22) He responds to the three *Sārparājñī* verses six times mentally. (23)

Therefore, the recitation, or the commencement of the *stotra*, is performed mentally by the *prastotṛ*, the *udgātṛ*, and the *pratihartṛ* with the *Sārparājñī* verses. 18 || 19 || 20 || 21 || 22 || 23 ||

If he recites by half-verses, the response for the Daśahotṛ formula is "O Hotṛ! nine times; for the Caturhotṛ formula, it is "So be it" (tathā); for the Pañcahotṛ formula, it is "Om"; for the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula, it is "So be it"; and for the Saptahotṛ formula, it is "We have succeeded, O Hotṛ" (arātsma hotar). || 24 ||
In this manner, the response (*pratigara*) is performed mentally; Baudhāyana and others maintain that both the recitation (*śaṃsana*) and the consecration (*anumantraṇa*) are likewise mental.
The mental *āśruta* and *pratyāśruta*, the *yājyā*, the *saṃpraiṣa*, the *vaṣaṭkāra*, and the *bhakṣa-mantra* [are performed mentally]. 25.

The responses *āśruta* and *pratyāśruta* are performed mentally. [The formulas are] "O Ukthaśas, sacrifice the Soma-libations" for the side of Soma, and "O Ukthaśas, sacrifice the Soma" for the side of Ākāśa. On the side of Ākāśa, it is done by means of the mind alone. At the end of the *yājyā*, there are the signs of the *vaṣaṭ* and *anuvaṣaṭ* calls. He carries away either the Soma or Ākāśa; the author of the Sūtra himself will state this later for the purpose of consumption (*bhakṣa*). || 25 ||

Having offered the oblation, they carry it away and consume it; whatever they look upon becomes subject to the rule of the invitation (*samupahava*). Sitting around the householder, they question him. (Section 9) 26.

1370 | ..... The Śrautasūtra composed by Satyāṣāḍha—[In the sixteenth Praśna]: On the following day, they carry forth the Soma or the Ākāśa for the purpose of consumption; those who are to consume it look at one another. There is a mutual invitation (*samupahava*) first mentally, then by the Hotṛ, and then by the Adhvaryu. The cup-bearers (*camasin*) consume their respective cups according to their designations. Having recited the mantra mentally, they consume the Soma directly with their eyes.

Regarding the portion for Ākāśa, the specific procedure for the consumption (*bhakṣaṇa*) is as follows: "Eat!... and so forth; "May [this] be dear to my heart"; "By the arms of the Aśvins, [I place] thee in the *sani*"; "Thee, who art the beholder of men, O divine Ākāśa"; "May I look upon thee with good vision"; "May the delightful, victorious speech, being pleased, satisfy Ākāśa," and so on. For the group, the formula is: "O deities of Ākāśa, knowers of the mind. Thus is the consumption. Having sat down, the discourses of the Brahman priest (*brahmakathā*) concerning the householder must be recited, beginning with: "Verily, by this alone, nothing whatsoever existed," and so forth. || 26 ||
"When the Daśahotṛs performed the sacrificial session, by what householder did they prosper? By what means did they create progeny?"—thus the Adhvaryu asks. (27)

Alternatively, having looked toward the householder, the great sacrificers sit around him on all sides and ask: "The *brahman* indeed [is] the four *hotṛ*s" (*Tai. Br.* 3.12.4). Since the office of *brahman* belongs to the four *hotṛ*s, the *adhvaryu* asks him first: "When the ten *hotṛ*s performed the sacrificial session (*sattra*)," and so forth.
"Indeed, with Prajāpati as their householder, they prospered; with him they created offspring," the householder replies. || 28 ||
The response. ||28||

"When the Caturhotṛs performed a sacrificial session, by what householder did they prosper? By what did they release the plants?"—thus asks the Brahman. "By Soma indeed as their householder they prospered; by that they released the plants," the Gṛhapati replies. "When the Pañcahotṛs performed a sacrificial session, by what householder did they prosper? By what did they drive away the Asuras from these worlds? By what did they win their cattle?"—thus asks the Hotṛ.

"By Agni as their *gṛhapati* they prospered; by him they drove away the Asuras from these worlds, and by him they won their cattle," the *gṛhapati* replies. "When the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ priests performed the sacrificial session (*sattra*), by which *gṛhapati* did they prosper, and by whom did they arrange the seasons? the Hotṛ-priests ask. "By Dhātṛ as their *gṛhapati* they prospered; by him they arranged the seasons," the *gṛhapati* replies. (16.4.30–31)
In every case, the response belongs to the householder alone. This is likewise even when [the interlocutor] is not inferior. 29 || 30 || 31 || 32 ||
They speak ill of Prajāpati. 33.
"It is known that they revile Prajāpati," thus says the Āpastamba Sūtra (21.11.13). ||33||
"This Prajāpati is unskilled, who would create gadflies and mosquitoes, as well as thieves. || 34 ||
The criticisms of Prajāpati are for the sake of propitiating Prajāpati; that is to say, for the purpose of liberation. 34.

Or rather, they recite the mantras concerning the censures of Prajāpati: "That which Prajāpati created—the wildernesses and the mountains—may Agni make that auspicious; may he bestow upon me that which is auspicious. That which the dawns, joined with darkness, heated upon your eye during the day, and the waters and the excessive heat—Prajāpati [made] those [auspicious] for you. That which [you have] other than wolves, gadflies, mosquitoes, and barley..."

"Then that which is crooked for you, that is their poison; by that, you [attain] immortality. 'May you partake of Prajāpati on the tenth day, the thought of the seers, the bull among men; bestowing a good dwelling and excellent wealth, free from evil, he establishes the one devoted to the gods in the world'—with these [verses] they should recite around him. || 35 ||

Regarding this, the Śruti says: "They explain that by means of this very [rite] they revile Prajāpati"; thus, the Mīmāṃsakas maintain that this is an explanatory passage (arthavāda) concerning the result. Alternatively, certain followers of particular Vedic branches recite mantras that revile Prajāpati; these [mantras] are to be accepted as authoritative. || 35 ||
Then he chooses a boon. || 36 ||
Immediately after the recitation concerning Prajāpati, the sacrificer chooses a boon. || 36 ||
"May there be food for us"—with whatever desire they perform [the rite], so it shall be. (Section 10) 37.
Thus ends the fourth chapter in the sixteenth book of the Sūtra of Satyāṣāḍha Hiraṇyakeśin.

"Bharadvāja says that one should utter the name of whatever one desires. Āpastamba says: "Furthermore, a Brāhmaṇa indeed has many desires" (21.12.1). The meaning is that one utters whatever one desires. || 37 || Thus ends the fourth chapter in the sixteenth book of the *Prayogacandrikā*, a commentary on the *Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-Sūtra* compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrin. 372. The *Śrautasūtra* composed by Satyāṣāḍha—[Book 16, Chapter 5] Now begins the fifth chapter in the sixteenth book.

Or rather, by this very formula—"bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ; may I be rich in offspring through offspring, rich in heroes through heroes, rich in splendor through splendor, and rich in nourishment through nourishments"—all their desires become fulfilled.
This mantra is for the purpose of desiring progeny; if desires do not exist, then it serves to remove the obstruction that has been incurred. || 1 ||
Having explained the Caturhotṛ formulas and closed the two doors, having seated the wives according to their respective hearths and closed the two doors, he then offers speech to them.

Having recited those four [verses], all [the priests], beginning with the sacrificer, close the two doors and take their positions according to their respective hearths (*dhiṣṇiya*), ending toward the north; likewise the wives sit down. Then the Adhvaryu offers speech to them with a clay vessel.

"Here is steadfastness, here is support, here is delight, here is pleasure"—saying this, they embrace the Udumbara post with their bellies, as it were, touching it; having taken hold of the Udumbara post together, they sit down. "O Indra and Parvata, you two who fight in the van, whoever shall attack us, him who comes against us, strike him down with the thunderbolt, strike each one of them down."

And they cast it far away, if it should fall into thickets; "O Hero, do thou, the best destroyer, crush our enemies on every side from all directions," [saying this], they all proceed while holding onto one another with their right hands, standing by the northern *havirdhāna* cart, passing over mats or reed-bundles. Having walked forward a little, they utter these five words: "Speech has come! Speech has come! Speech has approached! Speech has met us! Speech has come near to us! Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Thus they speak. 3.

Here, having embraced the Udumbara post with this mantra, "dhṛti," the sacrificers, maintaining silence, stand while holding onto it. It should be done in such a way that there will be contact with their bellies. Even in the Ahīna sacrifice, there is one [such instance]. Likewise, each wife stands silently; not all of them together. When the sun has risen above the trees, they move forward, holding onto one another.

Even when the Ahīna sacrifice is performed, there is only one [offering]; the ritual formula for the application is "O Indra and Parvata," and all proceed toward the north of the *havirdhāna* shed. Facing eastward, with their right hands joined and leaning on staves, they go forward and, to the north of the *āhavanīya* fire, utter five verses beginning with "Let speech come" (*vāgaitu*). || 3 ||

When the sun is above the trees, they release their speech with the Subrahmaṇyā call. (1.5) [This concludes] the Fifth Paṭala, together with the commentary *Prayogacandrikā* compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī. 373.
While the sun is still over the chest [of the sacrificer], the release of speech is performed by those moving in this manner, ending with the Subrahmaṇyā formula.
He places fuel-sticks of Udumbara wood upon the fire. || 5 ||

The release of speech occurs here for all those who have previously restrained their speech during the wrapping of the *audumbara* fuel-sticks. All the *audumbara* fuel-sticks have already been placed near the *āhavanīya* fire by the sacrificers. Then, on the tenth day, at the time of the *yajñāyajñīya* chant, the *vasatīvarī* waters and so forth are brought; this constitutes the continuity of the *ahīna* sacrifice up to the end of the spreading of the grass (*pārastaraṇa*).
On the following day, the *udayanīya* [offering] takes place; its form has already been explained. ||6||
The meaning has been explained. || 6 ||
The Prāyaṇīya and Udayanīya [offerings] exist here; there are no Ahīna continuations in this case. || 7 ||

On the following day, having understood [the procedure], they perform the *udayanīya* (concluding) sacrifice like the *prāyaṇīya* (opening) sacrifice. Both [the opening and concluding sacrifices] possess the *ṣoḍaśin* cup, because of the statement in another ritual manual (*kalpāntara*) that "the *ṣoḍaśin* belongs to the *atirātra* of the twelve-day rite. He brings down everything equally with the formula beginning "O Agni, lead us," and so forth. "I yoke the fire"—here, at the time of the silent pressing (*upāṃśu-abhiṣava*), the drawing of the *pṛśni-prāṇagraha* cups has already been explained. Regarding the *prāyaṇīya*, *udayanīya*, and the tenth day, three ritual options (*kalpa*) have been stated by the author of the Sūtra. Some say that these apply respectively to the three days.

Others say that there are conceptual constructions (*vikalpa*) everywhere. At the time for the animal sacrifice, the offering belongs to Agni; or, in the case of the eleven-fold set, he dedicates [the animal] at the *agniṣṭha* post, or to Indra-Agni. There is no fragmentation; for one desiring spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*), there is the instruction regarding the resting place for Sūrya. "A black antelope is your animal"—this is said day after day in the view of comparison. On the day of the *agnīṣomīya*, he measures one [post]. That, however, is the measurement on the *prāyaṇīya* day. He measures on that very [day]; he dedicates the animal to Agni, and the instruction regarding the resting place is to its south.

"On the following day, he dedicates the animal for Sarasvatī," and so forth; on the second day, he measures out the sacrificial post (*yūpa*). Because the post is for the sake of the animal, the sequence of the animals follows the primary order; thus, the ends of the posts are directed toward the south, not toward the north. The *upaśaya* (the horizontal log) is placed to the south of the post of Sarasvatī; this mention of the *upaśaya* occurs after the dedication of the animal to Sarasvatī. In this manner, each subsequent animal is dedicated day by day. In the case of the eleven posts (*yūpaikādaśinī*), it is as previously described.
On the preceding day, he takes the Vasatīvarī waters in preparation for the Yajñāyajñīya chant on the following day. ||8||
At the time of the sacrificial fee, while the Yajñāyajñīya chant was being performed, [he drew] the Vasatīvarī waters. || 8 ||
These constitute lineages that are not deficient. ||9||

This is established by logic from the statement, "In this [lineage], there are no deficient successions" (Saṃhitopaniṣad Brāhmaṇa 36.5.5). Thus, the expression "salutation be unto you" is indeed appropriate. || 9 ||
Moreover, having put on those very garments of the consecrated, they should proceed with the ritual.

They throw away the black antelope horn. When the *ṣoḍaśī* oblation has been performed, having proceeded with the night rounds (*rātriparyāya*), on the following day there is the release of speech (*vāgvisarga*) at the conclusion of the *tiroahniya* chant. There are eleven *samiṣṭayajus* offerings. Then, from the "tail of the sacrifice" (*yajñapuccha*) onwards, everything is like the *agniṣṭoma*. 10.
374 ...The Śrautasūtra composed by Satyāṣāḍha—...In the sixteenth book, at the time of shaving, they have their hair shaved including the top-knots when [the sacrifice] has become a Sattra. || 11 ||

When the omentum of the *anūbandhyā* cow has been offered, at the time of shaving, they shave their heads including the topknots—that is, they make them bald—as stated in the Śruti: "They shave following the topknot" (*TaiSaṃ* 7.2). However, in the case of an *ahīna* sacrifice, it is done excluding the topknot. Then follows the rite for the *pātnīvata* cup, and thereafter the rites beginning with the release of the fires.

At the Udavasānīya offerings, having chosen other officiating priests, they should perform separate sacrifices with them either by means of a Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, a Pṛṣṭhaśamanīya sacrifice with a thousand-fold dakṣiṇā, or one in which all one's possessions are given as the dakṣiṇā.

The ritual concludes with the *udavasānīyā* sacrifice, as in the *agniṣṭoma*. The *saktu-homa* belongs to the *gṛhapati* alone; everything else is as before. After all have performed the *udavasānīyā*, each sacrificer, having chosen sixteen other priests, should perform the *pṛṣṭhaśamanīya* sacrifices separately. Some do not desire the full set of rules for the *pṛṣṭhaśamanīya*. The formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) is: "I shall sacrifice with the *pṛṣṭhaśamanīya* at the next *parvan*. The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is one thousand. In that regard, the *traidhātavīyā* is fixed for both occasions.

Some do not accept [this]. On the immediately following festival day, there is either the Sautrāmaṇī or the Maitrāvaruṇī sacrifice. In this way, the arrangement of that which consists of the Sattra is completed. 12.
The twelve-day rite is concluded. (kha11) || 13 ||

[The sacrifice] has proceeded. The activity [of the sacrificers] is out of fear of the three worlds; however, some wise men do not accept that. The Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice should take place, and likewise the Vayasyā sacrifice; therein the Samūḍha-sattra is established. Now the ritual procedure for the Gavāmayana is stated:
by means of the Gavāmayana they go to Prajāpati, the Infinite, and they find firm footing in these worlds.
The place is in the earth. || 14 ||
The ritual procedure for that [twelve-day sacrifice], which constitutes a sacrificial session (sattra), has been explained by means of the twelve-day rite. || 15 ||
Having observed the specific excellence of that twelve-day rite, he states another alternative: "They should undergo initiation four days before the full moon. (16)

They should undergo initiation (*dīkṣā*) on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight four days prior to the full moon of Māgha. This being so, since the twelve initiations are completed on the new moon of the dark fortnight of Māgha, the purchase of Soma (*somakraya*) occurs on the immediately following Ekāṣṭakā. But is it not stated in the Gavāmayana: "If they undergo initiation four days before the full moon, their purchase of Soma falls on the Ekāṣṭakā" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.4.9)?

One should undergo initiation (*dīkṣā*) four days before the full moon; one should begin the initiation on the eleventh day. This being so, the twelve initiations conclude on the seventh day after the full moon. Consequently, the purchase of the Soma (*somakraya*) takes place on the eighth day thereafter. Since no specific rule is observed in this regard, any full moon day may be used.

Fifth Paṭala: Accompanied by the commentary *Mayūkhacandrikā* compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī. The first position is that [the initiation] should take place on the full moon of Citrā; for it is praised [in the scripture]: "They should undergo initiation on the full moon of Citrā, for the full moon of Citrā is indeed the mouth of the year" (*Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa* 7.4.9). Thus, the second position is that it should be on the full moon of Caitra. According to the technical terminology of the ritualists (*yājñika*), the eighth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha is the *Ekāṣṭakā*. On the eleventh day preceding the full moon of Māgha, the initiation (*dīkṣā*) should be commenced so that the purchase of Soma (*somakraya*) may be accomplished.

Those who have performed the first sacrifice with twenty-four as the maximum number of offerings, having offered the morning *agnihotra* on the *ekāṣṭakā*, attain spiritual knowledge (*vijñāna*). Regarding the passage beginning with "on the *ekāṣṭakā* that ordains the days" (*ahāṃ vidhānyāmekāṣṭakāyām*, *Taittirīya Saṃhitā* 3.3.8), the *ekāṣṭakā* is the ordainer of the days of the year-long sacrificial session (*saṃvatsara-satra*); on that day, the initiation (*dīkṣā*) takes place.

On the Ekāṣṭakā day, in the morning, having baked a cake made from flour measured by four śarāvas, and taking that cake as well as a firebrand, one should place the cake in a thicket and burn the thicket with the firebrand. If it burns, it is equal to merit; he remains free from calamity for a year. If it does not burn, it is equal to sin; it causes affliction through hunger and the like. They attain this knowledge. Having thus acquired this knowledge, the commencement of the Gavāmayana sacrifice takes place.

"It should be performed either with the *agnicityā* (the piling of the fire-altar) and the *gavāmayana*, joined with the *nāciketa* [fire-altar], or wherever the greatest number of oblations (*āhuti*) are offered. Because of the statement, "In this *gavāmayana*, the greatest number of cups (*graha*) are not drawn," [it follows that the *nāciketa* is required]. Even in the case of the *nāciketa* option, the initiation (*dīkṣā*) occurs on that same day. Āpastamba also says, "They should undergo initiation on the *ekāṣṭakā*. Having formed the resolve regarding this *ekāṣṭakā*: "Having made this determination, we shall sacrifice with the *gavāmayana* together with the *agnicityā* for the sake of heaven"—this is the formal resolution (*saṃkalpa*).

According to the opinion of Āśvalāyana, the fruit is either the *prājāpatya* and other rites, or the attainment of all desires; for it is said: "Now, the Gavāmayana is for the sake of all desires. It is entirely like the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) which constitutes a sacrificial session (*satra*). In this view, the preparation of the fire-pan (*ukhā-sambharaṇa*) takes place on the new moon day, and there is either an animal sacrifice (*paśubandha*) dedicated to Vāyu or five animals. || 16 ||
And on the full moon day of Māgha or Caitra. || 17 ||
On the eleventh day prior to the full moon of Caitra, the initiation (dīkṣā) is performed with the Agnivaddīkṣaṇīyā offering. In this manner, there are twelve initiations. 17.
On the coming eighth day is the Prāyaṇīya; regarding that, he says:

"The Prāyaṇīya is an Atirātra, the Caturviṃśa is an Ukthya, and the Ārambhaṇīya is a Trivṛt. There are two days consisting of two [sets of] Jyotis: the Agniṣṭoma with the Rathantara-sāman, the Ukthya with the Gaur-sāman, the Ukthya with the Bṛhat-sāman, the Ukthya with the Āyu-sāman, the Ukthya with the Rathantara-sāman, the Ukthya with the Gaur-sāman, the Ukthya with the Bṛhat-sāman, the Ukthya with the Āyu-sāman, the Ukthya with the Rathantara-sāman, and the Agniṣṭoma with the Jyotis-sāman and the Bṛhat-sāman. || 18 ||

On the eighth day, having performed the *prāyaṇīyā* [opening] sacrifice, the ritual beginning with the purchase of Soma follows. Relying on the bright fortnight of Caitra, the procedure is as follows: on the upcoming fourth day, the *agnīṣomīya* animal sacrifice takes place. On that day, they set up eleven sacrificial posts (*yūpa*). At night, the rites conclude with the spreading of the grass (*paristaraṇa*). When dawn breaks, at the great hour of night (*mahārātra*), one awakens and proceeds as in the *dvādaśāha* sacrifice, beginning with the formula "O Agni, lead us... and so forth. They perform the *prāyaṇīya-atirātra*. Here too, some do not accept the *pṛśni*, the *prāṇagrahas*, and other such elements, based on their specific names. The sequence begins with the cup for Indra and Vāyu (*aindravāyavāgra*). At the time of the animal sacrifice, there is either one for the *aikādaśina* animals of the modified sacrifices (*vikṛti*), or one for the *āgneya*.
376. *Satyāṣāḍha-viracita Śrautasūtra*—[16th Praśna]:

On the following day, the *tirohiyānta* (concluding rites with the *tirohīya* chant) and the continuities (*saṃtati*) are like those of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*). Like the second day of the *dvādaśāha*, there is the *caturviṃśa* *mukthya* as the introductory rite (*ārambhaṇīya*); having spread the sacrificial grass, there is no *anatigrāhya* cup, but the *śukrāmanthin* cups. At the time for the animal sacrifices, there is a ewe for Sarasvatī. The ritual concludes with the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings. On this day, which is designated as a *sattra*, the continuities of the *ahīna* sacrifice are performed as before. || 18 ||
The Abhiplava is a six-day period. || 19 ||
The word "they approach" is to be supplied as the ellipsis. || 19 ||
In this manner, four *abhiplava* periods are prescribed. || 16.5.20 ||

For those *abhiplava* periods, they perform the *jyotiṣṭoma-agniṣṭoma* with the *rathaṃtara-sāman*. [The *āgrayaṇa* cups are offered. At the time for the animal sacrifice, there is a brown (*babhru*) victim dedicated to Soma. In this manner, the *vyanīkā* sequence revolves until the *viṣuvat* day. (1) The *gaur-ukthya* has the *bṛhat-pṛṣṭha* chant; however, there are no *atigrāhya* cups. At the time for the animal sacrifice, there is a speckled (*śmāma*) victim dedicated to Pūṣan. (2) The *āyuṣa-ukthya* has the *rathaṃtara-sāman*, but there are no *atigrāhya* cups. At the time for the animal sacrifice, there is a white-backed (*śitipṛṣṭha*) victim dedicated to Bṛhaspati. (3) The *gaur-ukthya* has the *bṛhat-pṛṣṭha* chant.

At the time for the animal sacrifice, there is a *śilpa* (artistic) offering to the Viśvedevas. Then, at the time for the animal sacrifice, there is an Ukthya sacrifice dedicated to Āyus, with a reddish-brown animal for Indra. Then they undertake the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma with the Bṛhat-sāman; at the time for the animal sacrifice, there is a spotted animal for the Maruts. These [sacrifices] end with the Patnīsaṃyājas. They undertake four such Abhiplava periods. The remaining [days] consist of the Ekādaśinī.
The six-day period consisting of the *pṛṣṭhya* is the summary. || 21 ||
Of the eleven [animals] belonging to the Aikādaśina group. || 21 ||
He has a second, a third, a fourth, and a fifth; the sixth is to be supported. || 22 ||
In this manner they maintain the fires for five months; thereafter, [the fire] is to be brought together, so says Āpastamba. 22.
There are three *abhiplava* days. || 23 ||
The repetition of the *abhiplava* days and the sets of eleven-day periods is as in the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*). || 23 ||
The Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha. || 24 ||

The word "is said" (*ucyate*) is the ellipsis [to be supplied]. On either the latter three days or the former three days, the *Atigrāhya* cups dedicated to Agni and the others are offered. Thus, even when there is no formal completion (*asaṃpatti*), the consumption of honey and other rites take place at the end of the *Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*. || 24 ||
The three Abhijits are Svarasāman Ukthyas, or they are Agniṣṭomas.

Having performed these five months in this manner, they proceed immediately thereafter with his *saṃmārya* and the *pṛṣṭhya* month. Then follow three *abhiplava* periods, then the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, the *Abhijit*, the *Agniṣṭoma*, three *Sāman*-based *Ukthya*s, or *Agniṣṭoma*s.
The other two lie for two days. || 26 ||
The other two are the Śaya days. Among the four parts, the Atirātra is employed first. || 26 ||
Thus [end] the six months. || 27 ||

Six months are counted. Here, the counting is merely as follows: six months [are calculated] for those who perform the *paraḥsāman* and *ukthya* sacrifices interspersed with *agniṣṭomas*, resulting in a twenty-one-day period (*ekaviṃśatyaha*), according to the specific tradition of the Chandogas. For those performing nine-day *agniṣṭomas*, [the calculation is as follows]... [Fifth Paṭala].
This is accompanied by the commentary titled *Prayogacandrikā* compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī. 377.

The Ukthyas are those that perform the truth. Furthermore, there is a specific distinction regarding the *paraḥsāman* chants: among the *atigrāhya* cups on the first day, [the formula] "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the plants" is used for only one [cup], which is a modification of the [cup] dedicated to Agni. [The subsequent formulas are: "The plants are earthly," "This is thy womb; another [is] from the plants," "Waters, plants, thou art splendor"—in this way, "May you become [manifest] among the gods; make me full of splendor, long-lived, and radiant among men; and for the consecration (*dīkṣā*) thee," and so forth.

"Tejovindasīti" is according to the original formula. For the consumption [of the draught], one says: "May the clouds, may the progeny, may the waters and plants bestow splendor upon me. In the second *paraḥsāman*, one says: "I take you for the plants, for the progeny. These [formulas] are also modifications of those belonging to Agni. "This is your womb; for the plants, for the progeny," "The plants are full of splendor," "This god... and so forth—perform these among humans. And the consecration with "And for the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*)," etc., is as before.

"May wisdom be in me, may offspring be in me; may the plants bestow offspring and splendor upon me"—with these words, he consumes [the remnant]. At the third *paraḥsāman*, there is only one modification of the *āgneya* formula: "I take you, who are dear to offspring and to Prajāpati; this is your womb; for offspring, for Prajāpati. And the consecration with the formula, "O Prajāpati, you are full of splendor; may you be full of splendor among the gods; establish us among men," and so forth, is as before.

"May Prajāpati bestow intellect upon me, may he bestow progeny upon me"—with these words, there is the consumption [of the remnant]; at the end are the continuous sequences of the Ahīna sacrifices. || 27 ||
In the middle is the Viṣūvan, the twenty-first [stoma], the Agniṣṭoma Mahādivākīrtya. || 28 ||

Then they proceed to the Viṣuvat day: an Agniṣṭoma with twenty-one stomas, having the Divākīrtya as its Sāman. At the time of the ritual application of the Saumika vessels, beginning with the formula "O Agni, lead us," he sets out eight Atigrāhya cups.
Or [he uses] the Ādityavrata Sāman. 29.
The meaning is "they approach. || 29 ||
When the sun has risen, he begins the Prātaranuvāka.
He has gone. || 30 ||
This day is one on which the Divākīrtya hymn is recited. The northern wing is reversed; there are three Svarasāman days.

According to the principle that the constituent elements of a compound must be performed first, he draws the *śukra* cup starting from "O Agni, lead us... and so forth. If the *viṣuvat* day has the *jagat-sāman* chant, meaning it has the *divākīrtya-sāman*, then he draws the *āgrayaṇa* cup; at the time of the *atigrāhya* offerings, he also draws those not yet turned back. The performance for that is as follows: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the waters and the plants. And: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the plants and to offspring."

Having drawn [the draught] while facing upward with the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee for offspring, for Prajāpati," he recites the verse, "Upwards that [Sūrya]" (*udu tyam*), and then performs the setting down with the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee for Sūrya the radiant. Then he draws [the draughts] while turning back. With the formulas, "Support! For offspring, thee... (*upayāma prajābhyas tvā*), "Support! For plants, thee... (*upayāmauṣadhībhyas tvā*), "For offspring, thee, for offspring," and "Support! For [the gods] thee, for plants... and so forth as before, he draws them and performs the setting down with the words beginning with "I take thee" (*gṛhṇāmi*).

Then he draws the cup for Viśvakarman. Having recited the verse, "Vācaspati Viśvakarmāṇam... and the formula, "Upayāma... for Viśvakarman, svāhā, for the powerful one," [he says], "I draw what is pleasing. As in the case of Indra, [he says], "This is thy womb; for Viśvakarman, for the powerful one. At the time for the animals, he dedicates a white-backed animal to Bṛhaspati. Then he performs the dedication of an animal to Sūrya with the formula, "I dedicate thee, who art pleasing, to Sūrya," because of the statement, "He dedicates the animal to be offered at the Viṣuvat to Sūrya. In all cases, there is modification by means of the dual number.

At the time of the *atigrāhya* draughts, having recited [the formulas] for the upward [draughts] as before and performed the consecration (*anumantraṇa*), he then turns toward the solar [draught] from the return [portion]. Then [he offers] to Viśvakarman with the formula: "O Viśvakarman, full of vigor, may you be full of vigor among the gods. As in the case of Indra: "You are the knower of vigor; bestow wisdom upon me, offspring upon me, and Viśvakarman, bestow sensory power upon me. Thus the day concludes with the offerings to the wives (*patnīsaṃyāja*). These are the continuities of the *ahīna* sacrifice.

On the first day, at the time of the *atigrāhya* libations, one offers three *upayāma-graha* cups for the *ukthya* or *agniṣṭoma* [sacrifices] with the formula: "For offspring, thee; for Prajāpati," thus making one cup. On the second day, in the same manner, one offers the *upayāma-graha* with the formula: "For the waters, thee; for the plants. Among these, in the *agniṣṭoma*-connected [sacrifices], the first is the *āgrayaṇa* cup, the second is the *śukra* cup, and the third is the *aindravāyava* cup. In these, there is a continuity of the *ahīna* [sacrificial sessions]. || 31 || 32 ||
The Viśvajit sacrifice. || 33 ||

"One should perform the Agniṣṭoma," says Āpastamba. It begins with the cup for Indra and Vāyu (*aindravāyavāgra*), because there is no repetition [of the sequence]. At the time of taking the Āditya cup, he takes only the single Āditya cup; it has Aditi as its deity. Even in the Viśvajit sacrifice, though it possesses all the *pṛṣṭha* stotras, he takes only the single Āditya cup. Having recited "The great mother... (*mahīm ū ṣu mātaram*), [he uses] the formula: "Thou art the support for the Āditya, for the powerful one; this is thy womb, for Aditi, for the powerful one. O Āditya, thou art powerful; like the powerful Indra among the gods... [is not used here].

"May he bestow wisdom upon me, offspring upon me, and long life upon me"—thus [one should pray], for the continuity of the Ahīna sacrifice is maintained through the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings at its conclusion. || 33 ||
There are four types of *śaya* (lying) periods: the *ṣaḍaha* (six-day period) consisting of thirty-three *ārambhaṇas* (beginnings) and sixty [units]. 34.

Those four days of lying down [are observed] in the seventh month [with] the Gosava sacrifice. Then they enter upon the reversed *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*. The *trayastrimśa* is the beginning; the *āgrayaṇa* [cup] is the first. On this day, he takes the *vaiśvakarman* *atigrāhya* cup alone. There is a transposition of the *viśvajit*, the *nabhya*, the *āditya*, and the *vaiśvakarman*: in one case the *āditya*, in the other the *vaiśvakarman*. Thus, by way of transposition, he takes them from the *mahāvrata*; he takes each one individually, but does not employ the *ṣaḍaha* as a whole.

Now, the *dvitantra* itself begins with the *śukra* first; then the twenty-one-fold and sixteen-fold [stomas] are taken with the *aindravāyava* first; then the seventeen-fold with the *āgrayaṇa* first; then the fifteen-fold with the *śukra* first; then the nine-fold with the *aindravāyava* first. Thus the six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) is repeated. In the repetitions, there is one *anīka* (grouping) each; at the end of the subsequent six-day periods, there are the honey-eating rites and so forth.
Four Abhiplava [six-day periods] in reverse order constitute one month. || 35 ||
Having thus returned up to the Trayastriṃśa day, having reached the six-day period of the Pṛṣṭhya, and including four Abhiplava periods, that constitutes one month; that is one month. || 35 ||
6th Paṭala:
Accompanied by a second, accompanied by a third, accompanied by a fourth, and accompanied by a fifth. || 36 ||
Thus they attain what has been ordained. || 36 ||
The two Abhiplava [periods] are the highest when combined. || 37 ||

Then follows the *saṃbhārya* [arrangement]: in the uneven months there are two *abhiplava* periods; thus the *vyanīkā* [sequence] is reversed at the end. There is an *akṣīya* [decrease], followed by a *viśvajit*, and then an increase [of one day] up to the *viśvajit*. Those consisting of the *aindravāyava* draughts follow. The rest is understood. || 37 ||
The Gauh and Āyus are two days. || 38 ||

The *gavāyus* sacrifice; the *gośukrāgra*; the *āyurāgrayaṇāgra*. Alternatively, in the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, the *ukthya* day has the *aindravāyavāgra* sequence; then the *śukrāgra* day with the *rathaṃtara-pṛṣṭha* chant—thus Viśvakarman applies the *gavāyus* sacrifice, or else the sequence of precedence (*āgratā*). 38.
The twelve days of the Dvādaśāha [constitute] the twelve days. || 39 ||
The days following [the first] are twelve. || 39 ||
The Mahāvrata and the Udayanīya Atirātra [are the concluding rites]. (kha-12) || 40 ||

Thus ends the fifth chapter in the sixteenth book of the *Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-Sūtra*. The *Mahāvrata* and *Udayanīya* days are performed together as in the *Samūḍha* rite; thus, with four *Ahīna* sacrifices, a month is completed. In the *Dvādaśāha*, the first day has the *Aindravāyava* cup first, the second has the *Śukra* cup first, and the third has the *Āgrayaṇa* cup first. In this manner it proceeds. On the tenth day, the *Aindravāyava* is first. Of the ten-night *Daśarātra* of the *Dvādaśāha-Āhīna*, there are thirty-two *Ekādaśinī* animals for the seventeen-fold *Ukthya* sacrifice, which conclude the *Pārśva* (the side). Nine other days remain over; on those extra days, the additional animals are sacrificed.

The *gaṇya* (group) animal is for Viṣṇu; the *vāmana* (dwarf) is for Indra; the twenty-one cattle are for Indra; the *tṛṇava* is for the Viśvedevas; the thirty-three cows are for Heaven and Earth. Its calf is for the Chandomas; the cattle are for Aditi as the deity for the Maitrāvaruṇa cup, which begins with the Aindravāyava. At the Mahāvrata, there is a hornless bull for Prajāpati, beginning with the Śukra cup. At the *udayanīya* Atirātra, there is a bull for Agni, beginning with the Āgrayaṇa cup. || 40 ||
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the sixteenth book of the *Prayogacandrikā*, a commentary on the *Sūtra* of Satyāṣāḍha Hiraṇyakeśin, compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī.
16.6 Now begins the sixth chapter in the sixteenth book.

Twelve months constitute the Śāṭyāyanaka. Now, the meaning is that when the speech has been performed and the next day has dawned, they enter upon the Mahāvrata after having understood it. The Mahāvrata is for the sake of propitiating Prajāpati. There is the employment of the Saumika vessels beginning with "O Agni, lead us," etc. One employs thirty-seven *atigrāhya* cups. Thus ends the Śrautasūtra composed [in the sixteenth book].

— [He recites] *nakti*. With the two verses beginning with *uśāgneyān*, with the two verses beginning with *daśaindrān*, with the two verses beginning with *vaiśvakarmaṇādityau caivadra-sthāna*, they then pour out five vessels: one in each direction and one in the middle. Then, with the two verses beginning with *daśa sauryān*, he thus offers thirty-seven oblations. On this day, as in the archetype (*prakṛti*), he draws ten *āgneya* cups; as in the archetype, he deposits them with the two verses beginning with *sādanam*. He then draws ten *aindra* cups.

The setting down [of the cups] is according to their original nature; however, one should perform the Vaiśvakarman and Āditya [extractions] in combination, for the Śruti declares: "Both of these are taken together at the Mahāvrata. Five vessels are set down in the place of the Indra-vessel, one in each direction and one in the center. Therefore, there are seventeen Indra-vessels. Having performed the extraction for the Vaiśvakarman and Āditya, the extraction into the five vessels is as follows: in the eastern half of the vessel, he recites the introductory verse, "Indram id dhy avitāraṃ vṛṇīta."

Having released [the vessel] with the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Indra accompanied by the Ādityas," and having drawn it, he deposits it with, "This is thy womb; for Indra accompanied by the Ādityas, thee! This same procedure applies everywhere for the drawing and depositing of all five cups, including the one for Indra with the formula, "For Indra, thee, the companion of the hymns. For the southern half [of the altar], he uses, "We praise thee, O Hero"; for the western half, "Thee indeed we invoke"; for the northern half, "That indeed was the eldest in the worlds"; and for the central one, "That indeed was the eldest in the worlds."

Having thus poured all five [cups] that have been drawn into another vessel for the *savanīya* offering, he takes the whole into the middle cup, saying, "They choose thee at every season. Having said, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Prajāpati; this is thy womb; for Prajāpati thee," he sets it down. Then he draws ten [measures] for Sūrya; thus he concludes with the pair [of verses].
The upper wing is to be carried from both sides; it is the Tāṇḍaka.
The [offering] to Sarasvatī and so forth; now, according to some, there is an option regarding the northern side.

After the Viśvajit, there is a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha and three Abhiplava periods; thus, a month is completed minus two days. In the final month, which includes the *saṃbhārya* days, there are four Abhiplavas, the Gauḥ and Āyus days, and the ten days of the Dvādaśāha; this month is completed minus two days by means of the Mahāvrata and Udayanīya days. Now, according to the Bhāllavika school, in the first fortnight, before the first Pṛṣṭhya day, there is an Abhijit Agniṣṭoma.

In the latter alternative, after the final *pṛṣṭhya* [day] of the *viśvajit*, there follows a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period (*ṣaḍaha*) and an *āyus-ukthya*; that [last day] becomes a *gaura* in a single position. The rest is the same as the *Śāṭyāyanaka*. Now, according to some, it is known: "In a year-long sacrifice, they perform the *pṛṣṭhas* once; in the twelve-day (*dvādaśāha*) sacrifice, in the ten-night (*daśarātra*) period. There, in place of the *pṛṣṭhas*, there are *abhiplava* six-day periods.

After the twelve-night period, they proceed with the *daśarātra* and then perform the *mahāvrata*. (Section 13) 381. [This concludes] the first *paṭala*, accompanied by the commentary *Prayogacandrikā* compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrin.
He has gone. || 3 ||
On the following day, the twenty-five-fold Agniṣṭoma sacrifice with the Mahāvrata-sāman is performed.

"Pratāyate" means he begins; having set out the [cups] for Sūrya, he stops at the one for Sarasvatī, and so forth. At the time of the animal sacrifices, he immolates a hornless bull dedicated to Prajāpati with the formula, "I dedicate you, who are dear to Prajāpati," and so on. The performance of this Mahāvrata takes place together with the Marutvatīya offerings. || 4 ||
That which is prior to the Māhendra [offering]. || 5 ||
The meaning is that it comes into being; it exists before [it]. || 6 ||
When that has been performed, the Pratiprasthātṛ extends the ritual implements for the Mahāvrata.
When the Māhendra-stotra has been performed, the Pratiprasthātṛ [prepares] the Mahāvati-related crafts and implements.
There are ten highly refined [parts] of the neck of the lute. || 7 ||
The necks of lutes made from Udumbara wood become excessively worn out. || 7 ||
When each one has been thoroughly pressed, he weaves ten threads for each.

If, when these ten [threads] beginning with "staff" (daṇḍa) are established and each is further multiplied by ten, ten threads are woven into each one, that constitutes a hundred-threaded [cloth]. || 8 ||
That arrow consists of a hundred strands. || 9 ||
Vāṇa is a particular kind of lute. || 9 ||
They fasten the swing, which is above the seat of the Hotṛ, for the Hotṛ.
The Hotṛ priest mounts the swing (dolā) upon the plank (plekha). Thus [it is said]. || 10 ||
He places an udumbara stool for the Udgātṛ. || 11 ||
The Udgātṛ ascends the throne-seat. || 11 ||
The kūrca-grass mat and the wooden board are for the Adhvaryu priest. || 12 ||
He places it down; he follows along. || 12 ||
The Hotṛ priests and the Upagātṛs sit upon the bundles of grass. || 13 ||

"In the *kūrca* seats sit the *hotraka*s, the *upagātṛ*s, and the wives" (*Āpastamba Śrauta Sūtra* 21.17.15). This means that *kūrca* seats must be prepared for the *hotraka*s, the *upagātṛ*s, and the wives for the purpose of responding (*pratigara*); they should remain seated upon them. The *pratiprasthātṛ* should prepare these. What, then, are those [seats]? ... [Satyāṣāḍha-viracita Śrautasūtra, 16th Praśna] ... 302. Which indeed are those? ... [End of fragment]
All arts and crafts are fashioned therein. || 14 ||

Regarding this, Āpastamba specifies a distinction: "The wives take up the *apāghāṭalikās*, the *tālukavīṇās*, and the *piccholās*. The lute-players take up the lutes, the conchs, the *nālīs*, and the *tṛṇavans*. The religious student (*brahmacārī*) and the harlot (*puṃścalī*) take their places, entering through the southern door-arm of the *sadas*. (Āpastamba Śrauta Sūtra 11.17.16–18). And the musical instruments are [brought] together with the players. (14)

He unites it with the formula: "Truth is speech, the mind is auspicious; may that be auspicious for us, may there be auspiciousness for us. Having caused it to sound with a three-jointed *utkaṭa* splinter, or a bamboo joint, or a branch of *vetasa*, he begins the chant for Mahendra with a hundred-stranded arrow.
That is understood to be the staff (*daṇḍa*). He prepares it; he equips it. The rest has been explained. || 15 ||
It is a modification of the *barhis* grass.

And that staff is a substitute for the *barhis* grass; this is the meaning. Alternatively—with a stalk of sugarcane, a stalk of bamboo, or a stalk of reed—he performs the commencement of the *māhendrasya* stotra at the *sahya* sacrifice with the hundred-stringed lute (*vāṇa* or *śatatantu*), and at the *vahinī* [sacrifice] with the *bāṇa*.
|| 16 || The *udgātṛ*, having caused it to be played, hands it over to the *prastotṛ*. || 17 ||
The Udgātṛ gives it back again to the Prastotṛ. || 17 ||
The Prastotṛ [should give it] to the Adhvaryu. || 18 ||
The word "bestows" (prayacchati) is understood to carry over [from the preceding rule]. || 18 ||
The Adhvaryu hands it over to another. ||19||
To Vīṇāvāda, [salutation]. || 19 ||
He sits at the front of the assembly hall, near the southern door-post, striking it [with his staff]. || 16.6.20 ||
He stands at the southern door-post of the Sadas hall, striking it with the *śatatantu* mantra. || 20 ||
The wives sing along with them using apāghāṭalikā, tālukavīṇā, kāṇḍavīṇā, piccholā, and alābukapiśīrṣṇī lutes. || 21 ||

But is it not heard in the Mahāvrata: "The wives sing along (upagāyanti)"? In the archetype (prakṛti), it is heard: "The priests (ṛtvijaḥ) sing along. Thus, this singing by the priests is set aside by the singing of the wives. But is it not the case that in the archetype, while the Udgātṛ is singing the Sāman, other priests indeed sing along with the Sāman; whereas here, the wives play musical instruments (vāditram)? [End of] Paṭala 6. [From the] Payogacandrikā commentary compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrin. 383.

"There is no cessation [of the priests] because their spheres of activity are different. This is not so; for the word "singing" (*gāna*) is well-known to apply to the body. Therefore, when it is argued that the priests should be excluded and the wives should sing the *Sāman*, we reply: the meaning of the word "singing" is not the utterance of syllables, but rather the manifestation of musical tones (*svara*), and this is accomplished either by means of the body or by a musical instrument. For this very reason, those who know the true nature of singing say: "The wooden lute and the body-lute (*gātravīṇā*) are the two types of lutes among the various kinds of singing."

Furthermore, because that singing is an injunction for a new action according to the principle of *apūrva*, it would not possess the characteristics of the original model (*prakṛti*). If it is argued that, in that case, the word *upa* (meaning "accessory" or "additional") which denotes an increase in singing would be redundant, we say no; for an increase in the sound of the instrumental musicians (*vādinaḥ*) is possible. Indeed, there is the sound of the instrumentalists there, based on the scriptural text: "The drums resound in all directions. And the singing of the wives (*patnya-upagāna*) constitutes the sound of the instrumentalists, based on the scriptural text: "They sing along with flutes made of bamboo joints. Therefore, due to similarity and proximity, an increase in that [singing] is appropriate. Consequently, since there is no exclusion, there is a combination (*samuccaya*) of the two types of singing. || 21 ||
Playing [instruments], they cry out together; in all arts, they are third. || 22 ||
He has gone. || 22 ||
The unchaste woman and the celibate student meet together on the northern corner of the altar. || 23 ||
The religious student and the unchaste woman deliberate; standing before the sacrificial hall at the doorpost of the south, intending to repair it, some say, "We shall revile one another. (23)
The Māgadha and the Puṃścalu enclose [the area] at the southern corner of the altar. || 24 ||
On the northern corner of the altar, the Puraścālī and the Māgadha take up their positions; these two have already been explained. A union must be formed between these two.
They beat drums and produce continuous sounds in all directions.
Then they beat the drums; they blow them all at once. They fasten the drums in the directions, as if upon the corners of the sacrificial altar.
[The same applies] to the corners of the great altar. || 26 ||
The corner is the *srakti*. || 26 ||

To the west, having dug a knee-deep pit half within the altar and half outside the altar near the Āgnīdhra fire-hall, and having covered it with a moist hide and secured it with stakes, they strike the "earth-drum" (bhūmidundubhi) with the tail-end of the drum. || 27 ||

In another part of the Āgnīdhra shed, they dig a pit for the earth-drum (*bhūmidundubhi*). (The mouth-casing: Half inside the altar and half outside, having spread out a bull's hide with the hair side up using a mat, and having fixed it around with stakes, he places upon it the tail-end of that hide for the purpose of beating the earth. Or rather, they beat the earth-drum. The earth-drum has its mouth covered by a hide placed upon the ground; [it is beaten] with the tail-end. [Satyāṣāḍha-viracitaṃ Śrautasūtram—Chapter 16, Section 27]
To the north of the Āgnīdhra fire, a Śūdra and an Ārya struggle over a hide that has been prepared by a leather-worker. || 28 ||
Among Śūdras, there are both Śūdras and Āryas. An Ārya is a learned Brāhmaṇa; a Śūdra is well known [by that name]. || 28 ||
It is white, moist, and circular. || 29 ||
"The Pratiprasthātṛ must prepare the skin. This means that he should prepare a moist, white, circular skin for the purpose of the *carman* (skin). || 29 ||
The Brāhmaṇa stands within the sacrificial altar; the Śūdra stands outside the sacrificial altar. 16.6.30.
The word "remains" (tiṣṭhati) is to be construed with both [cases]. || 30 ||
"These have succeeded; these have accomplished what was real," so should a Brāhmaṇa say. "These have failed; these have accomplished what was evil," so should a Śūdra say. || 31 ||
The word "yad" (which) is to be construed with both [clauses]. || 31 ||
Having won it, the Brahmin spreads the skin upon the Āgnīdhra altar. || 32 ||
That [is] a Śūdra. || 32 ||
In front of the Āgnīdhra shed, he hangs it upon a bundle of mats—or, according to others, upon a bundle of reeds—after having stretched it out and raised it up. 33.

For that purpose, both of them, being hostile and each saying "this is mine, this is mine," stand apart. To the north of the *āśīda*, on a heap of straw or a heap of reeds—that is, in a place with much straw or a place with many reeds—they spread out the skin with a needle; having stretched it out, they raise it up. On a spot of the straw-heap, they fasten it like a fastening for the omentum (*vapā*) on a double-pronged fork. || 33 ||
In front of the Āhavanīya fire, princes wearing armor, having equipped themselves on chariots, move about with shields for the purpose of striking. ||34||
In front of the Āhavanīya fire, armored men gird themselves upon their chariots. || 34 ||
He instructs each one of them individually. ||35||
Of those princes. || 35 ||
"Do not let it fall short; do not let it overstep. || 36 ||
"Do not miss the mark; do not make your piercing elsewhere. Do not over-pierce; do not let the arrow go beyond," so he says, O wise one. 36.
Having pierced those, they cause them to fall down. || 37 ||
"According to some, the princes shoot [the arrows]," says Āpastamba. || 37 ||
Having gone northward to an unlimited space and having returned, they release [the cord]. || 38 ||
Arrows. || 38 ||

Eight young slave-girls, having placed water-pots upon their heads, go around the *mārjālīya* hearth three times clockwise while dancing, striking their right feet, singing this song: "May Vāgvedabhillukā sing for these; may she, being praised by the breath, sing for these sacrificers here. || 39 ||
Near the edge of the Mārjālīya shed, eight young female servants were dancing with water-jars. || 39 ||

They sing two *bhilluka* verses; two [verses] beginning with "Vāgvedahiṃvinī"; two [verses] beginning with "Vāgvedahastāvārām"; and two *saṃvatsaragāthā*. These are the *saṃvatsaragāthā*. || 16.6.40 ||

A mutual agreement was made between the male and female slaves: "The two Bhillukas shall sing; the two Vāgvedahimbins shall sing; the two Vāgvedahastas shall sing; the two Ārās shall sing; and the two Māthās shall sing for one year. (40)

Cows indeed are fragrant; cows have the scent of bdellium. Cows are the mothers of clarified butter; may they be most numerous here. Indeed, the cows of Maṅkīra drank the water of the Gaṅgā; they drank from the river Sarasvatī and waded into the eastern waters. We are floating on these like oars for one crossing over. Having scattered them for you in the midst, I shall pull them in like a fisherman with his nets. When Bheṅgya spoke to the Aśvins, "O you whose vehicle is the Ṛta, who did you slay?"

The censure of what has been revealed applies to both that which was done unintentionally and that which was done intentionally. When Rākhaṭya speaks of the vulgar Aṅkīra-dāśaka, while Kṣema and Vṛddha are in the village, the ox suffers by pulling for the sake of the village. This Kalmāṣya has breathed forth; this Soma has brought forth. This [is] the pinning with gold, this the breaking of the bones. "Haimahā! This Madhuhillu! Hillvahamaha! He measures the day. And all the Arāś hands attach themselves accordingly. 41.
