Having praised him, he is exhorted. || 44 ||
This is clear. || 44 ||
Standing on two bundles of grass or on two wooden boards, the Adhvaryu responds. || 45 ||

Beginning with "The sun is the purifier," the mantra ending in "the foundation" is stated in another Sūtra. The mounting of the wooden board by the Adhvaryu is accompanied by the muttering of the formula, "Come here, O so-and-so. Then the Adhvaryu responds to the recitation (*śastra*) as before. The Adhvaryu takes up the cup; thus the *āghāra* offerings are poured. There are ten *āgneya* cups as in the archetype, and ten *aindra* cups as in the archetype. Now, the two cups for Viśvakarman and Āditya have already been mentioned previously.

Then the Prājāpatya [oblation], consisting of five portions taken from the five vessels and placed together in a single vessel, he should offer. With the mantra "O Prajāpati, you are powerful among the gods," and so forth, there is a simultaneous offering according to the five-fold Indra-rite. Having bound them with a staff, there is an option regarding the *kokilī* [chant]. Having also bound the Āgneya and others with a staff, there is both the offering and the consecration (*anumantraṇa*). Having offered the Prājāpatya by way of a common procedure (*tantra*), he offers the Saurya oblations having bound them with a staff; the consecration is performed by way of a common procedure. The consumption (*bhakṣaṇa*) of all [the portions] is done separately, one by one.

Some [performers] combine all the Āgneya offerings into one, reciting "In me, wisdom... and so forth. Likewise, having performed the Aindrāgna offering, they then perform the Vaiśvakarmaṇa and Āditya offerings in sequence, followed by the Prājāpatya; in the five-fold view, these are separate. Otherwise (in the single-fold view), after looking [at the Soma] with the mantra "Bhadohi... and "Nṛcakṣasam tvā," they consume it with the words "...I consume. Then follows the consumption of the Saurya offerings separately, and then the Ukthya and so forth, according to the *tantra* as in the archetype. || 45 ||
The Great Vow is concluded. (Section 15) || 46 ||

Thus ends the sixth paṭala in the sixteenth praśna of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi Sūtra. The day concludes with the Patnīsaṃyāja. When the day has concluded, the specific rule according to Āpastamba is that the Brahman priest [recites] "vācam... The Mahāvrata [rite] concludes; the continuities of the Ahīna [sacrifices] have been stated. Thus ends the sixth paṭala in the sixteenth praśna of the *Prayogacandrikā*, a commentary on the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi Sūtra compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrin.
Now begins the seventh paṭala in the sixteenth praśna.
On the following day, the Udayanīya [offering] is explained. || 1 ||
Tomorrow, O great king, the Udayanīya Atirātra sacrifice will take place; it has been explained.
That which is the *prāyaṇīya* (opening offering) is also the *udayanīya* (concluding offering). ||2||
It becomes a rule. || 2 ||
In the three *paraḥsāman* days, he draws three *atigrāhya* cups.
On the three days that are about to be described. || 3 ||

"On the first day, he draws [the cup] with the formula: 'Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the waters and the plants. On the second [day], [he draws it] with: 'Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to the plants and to offspring. On the third [day], [he draws it] with: 'Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to offspring and to Prajāpati. He should draw these same [cups] in reverse order during the Arvāk-sāman days. ||4||
This is clear. || 4 ||

On the Viṣuvat day, he takes those [cups] both upright and not turned away; among them, he draws the seventh, the one for Sūrya, as the middle cup with the verse, "Upward that Jātavedas... On the Viśvajit day, he draws the cup for Viśvakarman with the verse, "The Lord of Speech, Viśvakarman, for our aid..."

On the following day, [the Adhvaryu] draws [the cups] with the verse "The great mother earth... for Āditya; these two [cups] are drawn alternately up until the Mahāvrata [day], when both are drawn together at the Mahāvrata. (6) Thirty-three *atigrāhya* cups are drawn on this day. (7) One may practice the modified (*vaikṛta*) cups by means of the original (*prākṛta*) ones, or the original ones by means of the modified ones. One should draw ten cups for Agni, (8) ten for Indra, ten for Sūrya, the two cups for Viśvakarman and Āditya, and the cup for Prajāpati. (9)

In the *pañcapātramati* vessel, four cups are placed in each of the cardinal directions, and the fifth is in the middle. (16.7.10–11) Having recited the verse "Indram id gāthinaḥ," he draws [the cup] in the eastern half with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Indra accompanied by the *arka*. He sets it down with the formula: "This is thy womb; for Indra accompanied by the *arka*, thee. (16.7.12) The drawing and setting down are identical everywhere. (16.7.13) [He draws the cup] in the southern half with the verse: "We praise thee, O Hero... (16.7.14)

"tvāmid dhi havāmahe" (We invoke you indeed)—this [verse] is at the rear half. "imā nu kaṃ bhuvanā sīṣadhema" (May we now bring these worlds to fulfillment)—this is at the northern half. (Section 16) "tad id āsu bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭham yato jajña ugras tveṣa nṛmṇaḥ | sadyo jajñāno ni riṇāti śatrūn" (That indeed is the eldest among these beings, from which the fierce and brilliant one was born; as soon as he was born, he, the truly victorious, destroys his enemies). Composed by Satyāṣāḍha, the Śrautasūtra, [Prapāṭhaka 16].

"He drives away the enemies; all the helpers rejoice after him"—thus [he recites] over the middle [cup]. Having poured those [liquids] together into a single vessel, he draws [the juice] into the middle cup, reciting: "They all turn toward the will in you," and then, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Prajāpati. He settles it with: "This is thy womb; for Prajāpati thee. If he were to offer them separately, he would cut off his own limbs; by pouring them together, he restrains the oblations, and accordingly the sacrificers restrain [their desires].

Only a small portion should be brought back to oneself and offered; thus one provides for the various limbs and does not obstruct the oblations. Having offered, he takes away the portion for consumption. He consumes it with the formula: "I consume your greatness; I consume your embryo; I consume your enjoyment; I consume your sustenance; I consume all of you, for the attainment of all, for the securing of all. || 17–18 ||

The *pṛśni*, the *prāṇagrahas*, and so forth [are performed]. In this context, there is the casting away of the black antelope horn (*kṛṣṇaviṣāṇā*) and the conclusion of the friendship (*sakhya*). However, these are not continuous sequences of an *ahīna* sacrifice. On the following day, up until the *atirātra*, the ritual tail (*yajñapuccha*) and so forth are performed like the *dvādaśāha* which has become a *satra*. Then, when the omentum (*vapā*) of the *anūbandhyā* cow has been offered, they shave their heads including the top-knots (*saśikha*). Having completed the *udavasānīyā* offering, they perform the *pṛṣṭhaśamanīya* rites individually and the *sautrāmaṇī* sacrifice. (5–18)
We shall now explain the threefold array. ||19||
The [section on] "Gone" is concluded. || 19 ||
The ritual procedure for these [vessels] has been explained by means of the ordinary *atigrāhya* cups. || 16.7.20 ||
Of those arrays. || 20 ||

The first day has the cup for Indra and Vāyu (aindravāyava) as its opening; then the cup for Śukra; then the cup for Āgrayaṇa. In this manner, the three rows (tryanīkā) revolve from here upwards before the Viṣuvat day, and after the Viṣuvat day, they revolve again and again in their reversals.

In the *Gavāmayana*, because of the commonality of the six-day periods (*ṣaḍaha*) in the *Abhiplava* sections, there is a six-day period consisting of the *Pṛṣṭhya* chants. In the first three-day period, or in the latter [three-day period], the *Atigrāhya* cups should be offered in that same manner. Some explain that "Jyotis," "Go," and "Āyus" are their respective names. The *Gavāmayana* concludes. Regarding the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*), the *Kāṭhaka* tradition applies to the *Ahīna* form, based on the statement: "By the *Ahīna*, one attains all worlds; and also by the *Sattra*. 21–22.
8th Paṭala: With the *Mayūkhacandrikā* commentary compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī. 389.
Regarding the Viṣuvat day, Ātreya says it has the *śukra* cup first; Bādarāyaṇa says it is according to what was observed. (Section 17) || 23 ||

The [section on] "gone" is concluded. || 23 ||
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the sixteenth book of the *Prayogacandrikā*, a commentary on the *Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-Sūtra* compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī.
Now begins the eighth chapter in the sixteenth book: Next, the preparation of the sacrificial animal (*paśuklṛpti*). || 1 ||
The word "will speak" is to be supplied as the ellipsis. || 1 ||
At the Prāyaṇīya Atirātra, they sacrifice a goat dedicated to Agni; on the following day, a ewe dedicated to Sarasvatī.
The word "they sacrificed" (ālabhanta) is to be construed with both [clauses]. || 2 ||
In this manner, they slaughter the eleven animals prescribed for each day.
Every day, immediately.
Having come together again and again, they repeatedly perform the set of eleven offerings.
"The Saurya [oblation] is to be performed at the Viṣuvat day," so says the Āpastamba Sūtra.
As they thus perform the introductory rites for the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*), thirty-two sets of eleven sacrificial stakes (*ekādaśinī*) are concluded at the seventeenth *ukthya* day.
They take hold of those very [objects]. ||1||
Nine days are left over. || 6 ||
On the nine days. || 6 ||
Among them, those animals that do not exceed the number of cows. || 7 ||
The word "they sacrificed" (ālabhanta) is to be understood as the ellipsis. || 7 ||

The Vāmana for Viṣṇu on the twenty-first day; the Aindrāgna on the twenty-third; the Vaiśvadeva on the thirty-third. On the first Chandoma day, a milch-cow for Heaven and Earth; its calf, dedicated to Vāyu, on the middle one. [From the Śrautasūtra composed by Salyāpāda... An ewe for Aditi on the Avivākya day; a cow for Mitra and Varuṇa on the last one. A hornless bull for Prajāpati at the Mahāvrata. An animal for Agni on the Udayanīya day. Thus for the followers of the Pāliṅgāyana school. 8.
He has gone. ||8||
Now, the followers of the Kāṭhaka school offer the animals of the Ekādaśinī group at the Prāyaṇīya and Udayanīya sacrifices, either by distributing them or without distributing them.
The plural form "Kāṭhakāḥ" is used for the sake of honor. || 9 ||
The Āgneya [stotra] is used when there is concealment; the Aindra [stotra] is used for those sacrifices where the Rathantara is the Pṛṣṭha-stotra and the Bṛhat is the Pṛṣṭha-stotra.
"In rites where the *rathantara* is the *pṛṣṭha*-stotra, the offering belongs to Agni; in those where the *bṛhat* is the *pṛṣṭha*-stotra, it belongs to Indra"—thus says the Vaikhānasa-sūtra.
Alternatively, one may offer an oblation to Agni-Indra when the Rathantara is the Prstha-stotra, and to Indra-Agni when the Bṛhat is the Prstha-stotra.
The phrase "or rather" (api vā) is intended to indicate the opinion of another Vedic school. || 11 ||
At the Viṣuvat day, they immolate a victim for Sūrya, and then additional victims for the cattle.
In those same nine [vessels], the Gavya [libations] are offered.

On the thirty-third day, there is a white-backed animal for Bṛhaspati; on the first day of the Chandomas, a milch-cow for Heaven and Earth; on the middle day, its calf for Vāyu; on the last day, a dappled cow for Speech; on the Avivākya day, an animal for Mitra and Varuṇa; and on the Mahāvrata day, a hornless bull for Viśvakarman—so says the Vājasaneyaka.
The grammatical connection is that they "took hold" everywhere. || 13 ||

At the Agniṣṭoma, they immolate an animal dedicated to Agni; at the Ukthya, a second one dedicated to Indra-Agni; at the Ṣoḍaśin, a third, a ram dedicated to Indra; and at the Atirātra, a fourth, a ewe dedicated to Sarasvatī—so say some teachers. If these animals were available, they should immolate them in this very manner day after day.
The meaning is clear. || 14 ||

If they proceed with the eleven animals, on the first day they should immolate only the one dedicated to Agni; then the others in successive order as before, with the ram for Varuṇa being the last. On those [subsequent] days, they should immolate only the one dedicated to Agni on the first day; then the others in successive order as before, with the ram for Varuṇa being the last. By means of these very [animals], they should proceed in reverse order. (Section 18) 15.
[Paṭala 8] Accompanied by the *Prayogacandrikā* commentary compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī.

"Or an Aindrāgna [animal sacrifice] everywhere," says Āpastamba. "If there is the means, they should offer the animal sacrifices every day, adding them together; or [they may offer] the Ekādaśina animals distributed [throughout the year]," so says Bharadvāja, according to the Vājasaneyaka (BaudhŚS 21.23). The rest has been explained. Now the ritual of the Utsargiṇāmayaṇa is stated:
"We shall explain the Utsargiṇāmayaṇa. (16)
"Utsargiṇām ayana" is the name of a ritual action.
It has been explained by means of the Gavāmayana sacrifice. || 17 ||

The Gavāmayana itself is modified by specific qualities, like the Dākṣāyaṇayajña. Having specified the fruit as being like that of the Gavāmayana—saying, for example, "We shall sacrifice with the Gavāmayana-Utsargināmayaṇa; may I attain Prajāpati"—some state the fruit to be longevity, cattle, and heaven. Others say, "We shall sacrifice with the Utsargināmayaṇa for the sake of long life, for the sake of sons, for the sake of cattle, or for the sake of averting a fall into hell"; in all these cases, it is like the Gavāmayana. || 17 ||
In that regard, he shows a certain deliberation for the sake of a definitive decision: "They should omit the full moon day and the new moon day of the year. (18)

"Should it be released? Or should it not be released? (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.6.7). Having kept in mind these two defects—the interruption of the sacrifice in the case of releasing [the breath], and the suppression of the breath in the case of not releasing it—the exponents of Brahman deliberate. The protracted vowel (*pluti*) is for the sake of deliberation. In this regard, the experts, because the interruption can be remedied by means of sacrificial animals dedicated to Prajāpati and the like, have determined that the option of releasing [the breath] is indeed superior, in order to avoid the suppression of the breath.

He indicates that very specific day with the words: "On the new moon and on the full moon, it should be relinquished" (7.5.7). It is well known that these two, the new moon and the full moon, are occasions for sacrifice. Therefore, the determination is that whatever day falls on those two lunar days, that day should be relinquished. || 18 ||

Now he states the position of others: they should either undertake those [rites] or not abandon them; they should perform that very same [rite] on the following day. At the end, they should abandon either the new moon (amāvāsyā) or the full moon (paurṇamāsī). On the final day, the Bahiṣpavamāna chant is the Trivṛt, with the verses: "O Vāyu, the bright one," "He has come," and "This one, the ten fingers. || 19 ||

Therefore, their abandonment is not proper. (19) Having thus clarified the abandonment, he clarifies the specific details regarding what is to be performed therein: "On the day they should abandon [the fires], on that very day they should perform an *iṣṭi* sacrifice; either two *puroḍāśa* cakes for Agni and Marutvat, or those for Indra-Viṣṇu, or those for Indra-Bṛhaspati, or those for Indra-Viśvedevas, or according to the ritual rules of the *adhvara*. (16.8.20)
Then, on that day of disposal, they should offer four oblations.
From the *Śrautasūtra* composed by Satyāṣāḍha—[16th Praśna]:
Among them, those who offer the *puroḍāśa* cakes observe the fast; those who offer the *sāṃnāyya* milk-offering set aside the calves on this day, as do they for the animal sacrifice.
Of those ritual procedures for the sacrifice. || 21 ||
The Prājāpatya penance consists of [subsisting on] milk products. || 22 ||
According to the Vedic scripture, "They sacrifice an animal dedicated to Prajāpati" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.5.7), [the offering consists of] milk in the case of the rite of renunciation. || 22 ||

As for the Vaiśya, so [are the offerings] for the Tāmasa: sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśas*) for Indra accompanied by the Vasus, for Indra accompanied by the Haris, and for Indra accompanied by Bṛhaspati and the Viśvedevas. There are eight, eleven, and twelve potsherds (*kapālas*) respectively, in due order. The times for the pressings (*savanakāla*) have also been explained.

Just as Agni accompanied by the Vasus is the lord of the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*), so Indra accompanied by the Maruts is the lord of the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina-savana*). That Agni possesses the Vasus is to be understood from the Brāhmaṇa: "When they offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni accompanied by the Vasus at the morning pressing, and curd to Indra; indeed, the midday pressing belongs to Indra accompanied by the Maruts. When they offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra accompanied by the Maruts..."
"The third pressing belongs to all the gods accompanied by the Ṛbhus; therefore they offer a cake on twelve potsherds dedicated to the Viśvedevas" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.5.7). || 23 ||
"Those who have abandoned [their calves]," they say, "are those who deprive their calves of milk. || 24 ||
"When it becomes curd" (7-6-7), so says the Brāhmaṇa. || 24 ||

In the morning they immolate the animal; they proceed with its omentum. Then follows the cake for the Viśvedevas on twelve potsherds. The third-pressing oblation of cooked rice for the Viśvedevas is completed. When the offering of speckled butter has been performed, they cause the wives to sacrifice together; they cause the wives to sacrifice together. (Section 19) ||25||
Thus ends the eighth chapter in the sixteenth book of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-sūtra.
Thus ends the sixteenth book of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-sūtra.

Now, this is the procedure: having performed everything up to the *dīkṣā* and *upavasatha* rites as in the *gavāmayana*, they perform [the rites] from the *prāyaṇīya-atirātra* until the end of the first month; that is to say, the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*.

At the conclusion of the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings, having performed the consumption of honey and other rites, and having taken the *vasatīvarī* waters from the northern fire, he performs the rites for the curd for Indra, beginning with the fetching of the branch and ending with the smearing of the pot. Having carried the *vasatīvarī* waters around at night and placed a lump of clay within them, he performs the rites beginning with the strewing of grass. Having recited "O Viṣṇu, [accept] the oblation," he prepares the curd for Indra and adds the fermenting agent (*ātañcana*) using rice grains. The five milkings and so forth are not performed. Having done this, he observes the fast. On the following day, he proceeds according to the order of the vehicles.
In that [sacrifice] or in the Gavāmaya, there is an omission. There is an omission of the Jyotis day, which is the first of the Abhiplava days. Its substitute is an animal dedicated to Prajāpati.
[End of] Paṭala 8, accompanied by the commentary *Prayogacandrikā* compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrī. 393.

They perform those [rites], such as the fetching of the two branches and so forth, like the *savanīya* sacrifice. The taking of the clarified butter (*ājyagrahaṇa*) occurs either on the *prastara* grass-bundle or on the furrow made by the wooden sword (*sphya*). Having performed the rite with the formula "I employ the three, O Viṣṇu," and having encircled the *agniṣṭoma* with the threefold cord (*trivṛt*), and having untied it, he dedicates [the animal] as in the *vājapeya*: "I dedicate [this] which is dear to Prajāpati. At the morning time, having proceeded with the omentum (*vapā*), it continues until the measuring. They offer a cake on eight potsherds (*aṣṭākapāla*) to Agni accompanied by the Vasus.

The setting out of the vessels and so forth is like that of the animal-cake (paśupuroḍāśa). One offers [the oblation] with the formula: "I offer what is pleasing to Agni accompanied by the Vasus. The ritual invocations (nigamas) begin with: "O Agni, accompanied by the Vasus, protect the oblation," and so forth. At the time of the circumambulation with fire (paryagnikaraṇa), some say that having brought the Sāṃnāyya for Indra, one performs the circumambulation for both together with the animal-cake. Having performed the touching of the placed [vessels], one proceeds with the animal-cake, and then proceeds with the offering to Indra.

For these two [offerings], the rites beginning with the *sviṣṭakṛt* and ending with the *iḍā* and the *mārjana* are common. Having invited one another, they consume the *sānnāyya*. The invitation consists of the sacrificers saying, "Invite us," and [the others] responding, "Do invite. The consumption is performed silently. Some desire this to be like the consumption of Soma, based on the Śruti text: "For this is indeed a draught of Soma. Others perform the specific rites of bringing the branch (*vaiśeṣika-śākhāharaṇa*), the fourfold division (*caturdhākaraṇa*), the smearing of the flour (*piṣṭalepa*), the husks (*phalīkaraṇa*), the release of the potsherds (*kapālavimoka*), the wiping of the *praṇītā* water (*praṇītāmārjana*), the removal of the *upaveṣa* stick (*upaveṣoddhāsana*), and so forth.

When midday has arrived, having performed the animal sacrifice (paśupuroḍāśa) up to the end of the iḍā-portion—[offering] a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra accompanied by the Maruts (marutvat), and a pap (caru) for Indra—the placement of the vessels and so forth follows. The ritual formulas (nigamas) are: "For Indra accompanied by the Maruts, acceptable," "For Indra, acceptable," "O Indra accompanied by the Maruts, protect the offering," "O Indra, protect the offering," and so forth. Having performed everything up to the touching of the placed offerings, [the rites] proceed from the oblation of the sacrificial food (havirāhuti) up to the cleansing of the iḍā. At the time of the third pressing (tṛtīyasavana), the sacrificial food is cooked. 3.

Having performed the ritual with the animal sacrifice beginning with the *śamitṛ* (the slaughterer) and ending with the wiping of the *iḍā*, he offers a twelve-potherd oblation (*dvādaśakapāla*) to the Viśvedevas and a pap (*caru*) to the Viśvedevas. From the setting out of the vessels up to the touching of the placed items, the offerings of the sacrificial materials are cast into the fire by way of a single performance (*tantra*). In the animal sacrifice, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings are obligatory. Alternatively, in place of these sacrificial materials, he offers the *savanīya* animal-cakes according to the *adhvarakalpa* procedure, beginning with "To Indra Harivat," or the cake on eight potsherds for Agni-Viṣṇu, and so forth.

At the *savana*, there is a cake on one potsherd for Mitra and Varuṇa; this is found in all ritual systems. There is an animal sacrifice dedicated to Prajāpati. The animal rites beginning with "O Agnīdh, perform the *upayaj* offerings" and ending with the *patnīsaṃyāja* are as before. The drawing of the *vasatīvarī* waters is also already performed previously. For the subsequent day, the fetching of the branch and so forth constitute the continuity of the *ahīna* sacrifice. At night, the rites conclude with the strewing of grass (*paristaraṇa*). Some authorities desire that the entire procedure of the animal sacrifice to Prajāpati be completed.

When the next day has dawned, at the great night, having awakened, [he performs the rites] beginning with "O Agni, lead us... and "The cow, the Ukthya, the Bṛhat-sāman... and so forth. In this manner, after completing and filling out the months consisting of the six-day periods (*ṣaḍaha*) from here onwards, there is the *utsarga* (conclusion). That which was the first month consisting of the *abhiplava* periods, known as *jyotis*, that indeed must be omitted. When the days have been concluded, they perform the animal sacrifice for Prajāpati, those for Agni Vasumat, and so forth, during the early part of the night; and everywhere they perform the preparation of the curd and the depositing of the clod of earth in the *vasatīvarī* waters.

Before the *Sviṣṭakṛt* offering, five *jyotis* days are omitted; after the day of the flour-offering (*piṣṭavat*), the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* and subsequent rites follow. Four *bhūta* days consisting of *trayastrimśa* stomas are omitted.
(Satyāṣāḍha-viracita Śrautasūtra, Mahāgnisarvasva-prayoga-caryā-saṃgraha, Chapter 16, Section 850).

[They perform] the Vyānis. For five months, there is no omission of the *bhūta* [Sāman] consisting of the *trayastriṃśa*. There is an omission of the *jyotis* [Sāman] known as the *saṃbhārya*, which consists of the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* and so forth. Now, according to the view of some, there is an option in the *Āpastamba-sūtra*: "The stotras have a single performer," and so on. Having omitted [the Sāmans] in this manner, and having performed the *udayanīya-atirātra* sacrifice, they emerge from the *avabhṛtha* bath; having completed the rites beginning with the *udayanīya* and ending with the *udavasānīya*, and having again performed the gathering of the fire-pans (*ukhā*) and so forth, and having been initiated, they should resume those [Sāmans] that were previously omitted.

There are no *prāyaṇīya* and *udayanīya* [sacrifices]. Thus [the sequence continues] up to the *udavasānīyā*. Then, by means of a common ritual framework (*tantra*) for both, there follow the *pṛṣṭhaśamanīya*, the *sautrāmaṇī*, and the *maitrāvaruṇī*. The *tryanīkā*, the *atigrāhya*, and the eleven [cups] should be present during the *utsargiṇām ayana*. For that day on which the *utsarga* (release) is reached, there is simply the abandonment of the *savanīya* and the *atigrāhya* cups as they have been obtained.

Regarding the re-taking of what has been discarded and the discarding [of what was not], that which was obtained as an animal sacrifice and so forth—here (*iha*) this must be performed for the sake of longevity; this *sattra* is for the sake of sons, for the sake of cattle, or for the sake of heaven, and it is the cause for the cessation of the torments of hell. Such is the fruit for one who has modified the ritual according to these qualities. The repetition of the phrase "the wives perform the *saṃyājana*" is for the purpose of concluding the inquiry. Thus, in the commentary on the *Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-sūtra*, compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrin...

The eighth chapter in the sixteenth book of the *Prayogacandrikā*. ...This Kaustubha jewel, a definitive exposition (*nirṇaya*) of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*), has been fashioned here from the thread-arrangement of the garland of the *Prayogavaijayantī*. May it, placed by me in the center of the body of the Sacrifice, serve for its satisfaction; for it indeed accepts something from the devotee, and thus it has been composed. Thus ends the sixteenth book in the *Prayogacandrikā*, a commentary on the Sūtra of Satyāṣāḍha Hiraṇyakeśin, compiled by Mahādeva Śāstrin.
Now, in the seventeenth book, the first chapter:
the Agniṣṭoma is the archetype of all sacrifices.
But for those belonging to the schools, the first [alternative] applies everywhere. || 2 ||
Or as has been instructed. || 3 ||
The Trikadrukas are Jyotis, Gaus, and Ayus. || 4 ||
The first [day] is either an Agniṣṭoma or an Ukthya. ||5||
All [are present]. ||6||
"He gives a thousand [cows] at the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice. || 7 ||

By the rule of the Śyaita [sāman], the Bṛhat-pṛṣṭha [rite] is for one who has rivals; the Āyuḥ [rite] is for one desiring heaven; the Agniṣṭoma is for one who has rivals. The Viśvajit-Agniṣṭoma, containing all the Stomas and all the Pṛṣṭhas, is for one desiring preeminence; its sacrificial fees are a thousand, or alternatively, all one's possessions, or as many as there are Stotriya verses in the rite. (8)
Having excluded the eldest son from the distribution of all his property, he may make a private agreement with them. 9.
At the time of the sacrificial fee, he gives away his entire property. || 17.1.10 ||
Whatever else belongs to the Brahmins in the various directions, other than wealth, land, and armies. || 11 ||

Having brought the excellent sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) and having settled [the fire], or having sat down to the south of the Audumbarī pillar facing east, he should say: "Whatever debt I have here, all that I give away. || 12 ||

Having moved away, they put on a red cow-hide—complete with ears, tail, hooves, and dewclaws—as a protection against being spoken ill of; they wrap their heads with turbans and take up a cup made of Udumbara wood.

And [they take] a spade made of Udumbara wood, or of Khadira or Venu wood; it should be spotted, hollow or solid, and sharpened at both ends—or sharpened at one end only. Living on roots or living on fruits, they dwell for three nights in the forest by an Udumbara tree. Digging up a root with a digging tool while they are alive, and placing it in an Udumbara vessel, they eat it together, drinking from an earthenware cup. [They stay] three nights among the Niṣādas, three among the Vaiśyas, three among the Rājanyas, and three among the Brāhmaṇas, according to some teachers. (Section 1) 13.
For a year or for twelve days, he should not beg; nor should he refuse what is being given to him. || 14 ||

Indra’s sacrifice is the Abhijit Agniṣṭoma for the sake of conquering what has not been conquered. Both the Bṛhat and Rathantara [Sāmans] are used; or rather, they are used as the Pṛṣṭha-stotras in their indirect form.
But for the Hotṛ, there are eleven large animals at a single sacrificial post.
Or, for the excellent [vows], there are twelve hundred with a thousand-fold sacrificial fee. || 17 ||
By means of the Sarvajit Agniṣṭoma with all the Pṛṣṭha-stotras, one obtains everything and conquers everything. ||18||
And he becomes an eater of food. || 19 ||
For him, the Pṛṣthya Mahāvrata with the Arkya hymn is prescribed as the recitation.
The sacrificial fee is one thousand, or twenty-eight each for twenty [priests].
There are four thousand. || 22 ||

The *Jyotis-Agniṣṭoma* with the *Rathantara* as its *Sāman* is the first; it is the foremost of thousands. One becomes firmly established in the vital breaths and in the eating of food. The *Gauḥ-ukthya* with the *Bṛhat* as its *Sāman* is the second; one becomes firmly established in cattle. The *Sarvajyotis-Agniṣṭoma* with both *Sāmans* is the third; it is for the attainment of all and for the securing of all. The *Agniṣṭoma* equal to the three-night sacrifice (*Trirātra*), with either the *Rathantara* or the *Bṛhat* as its *Sāman*, or with both *Sāmans*, is the fourth. One obtains the fruit of the three-night sacrifice. || 23 ||
There are four Sādyaskra sacrifices.
Their distinction is as follows: || 25 ||

The first [sacrifice] has the *rathaṃtara* as its *sāman*, or the *bṛhat* as its *sāman*, or both as its *sāmans*. In that [first sacrifice], there are desires regarding the acquisition of Soma, preeminence, rivalry, or the desire to cross over for one who has enemies; [the results are] heaven or cattle. (Section 2) 26.
On the previous day, there were animals dedicated to Agni, Soma, and Bṛhaspati. || 27 ||

In the event that these [specified] deities cannot be obtained, there shall be, in their respective order, a cake on eight potsherds for Agni and two oblations of cooked rice (caru) for the other two.
He maintains the Āhavanīya fire. || 29 ||
He sprinkles the *uttaravedi* with clarified butter.
Eating food mixed with clarified butter. || 31 ||
Having placed gold in his mouth, he lies between [his feet] as one observing celibacy for the sake of his beloved wife. 32.
"I shall sacrifice with the iṣṭi. The officiating priests have already ascended [to their duties]. || 33 ||
Having deposited those [vessels], on the following day, messengers carrying horse-chariots, milk-filled leather bags, and Soma-proclaimers run out in all directions. || 34 ||
Whatever fresh butter (navanīta) arises from them, one should pour it into the clarified butter (ājya). || 35 ||

In the eastern direction, he should cause [the cart] drawn by four yoke-animals to travel for one *yojana*, and in the other directions, by releasing it at intervals of one *krośa* per yoke-animal; then, with a single-wheeled cart, he should cause it to circumambulate to the left. Alternatively, a chariot drawn by mules should perform one circumambulation to the right, or [he may perform] *yojana*s and so forth, or *krośa*s, to the right with a horse-chariot.
The general rule has been explained. || 37 ||
A three-year-old steer with testicles is the price for purchasing the Soma. || 38 ||
During the silent recitations (upasad), he should close his eyes three times.
Or he may perform [the rite] with his eyes closed. || 17.1.40 ||
The sacrificial altar is made of excellent barley soil. ||41||
The *yavānī* plant is the threshing floor; the *uttaravedi* is the threshing floor. || 42 ||
On ascending the Havirdhāna shed. || 43 ||
The hall is measured out. ||44||
The sacrificial post is a wooden sword, or it has the point of a wooden sword, or it is a threshing-post. || 45 ||
At the time of the offering to Agni and Soma, he prepares an eleven-potherd oblation for Agni and Soma. He takes the Vasatīvarī waters from the house of one who has performed the sacrifice.
At the time of the *savanīya* offering, he immolates the animals together. || 47 ||
The animal sacrifice dedicated to Agni and Soma, the Savanīya, and the Anūbandhyā. || 48 ||

In place of the animal sacrifice to Agni and Soma, one should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Agni and Soma; in place of the Anūbandhyā cow, one should sacrifice with curdled milk (āmikṣā) dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa.
A white horse that runs well is the sacrificial fee. || 17.1.50 ||
One should give it to a rival who is an Aṅgirasa. ||51||
Or, having chosen a Brahmin who is disliked, he should give him a white horse adorned with gold ornaments. || 52 ||

For a year he should not sit upon anything elevated; he should not eat meat; he should not approach a woman; he should not wash his feet, nor anoint them, nor rub oil on them. That is the consecration (*dīkṣā*). If he does not intend to complete it for a full year, [he should observe it] for twelve days. (Section 4) 53.
Thus ends the first chapter in the seventeenth book of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-Sūtra.
Now begins the second chapter of the seventeenth book.

Having made the twenty-first [stotra] the Agniṣṭoma-sāman of the second [form], one should cause one afflicted by disease to sacrifice; with this same [rite], one should cause one who desires food, or one who desires offspring, or one who desires cattle, to sacrifice.
It revolves by means of three [verses] each. ||2||
For the third [stoma], the fourteenth and eighteenth [verses] are the two subsequent *pavamāna* chants; or alternatively, the fourteenth and eighteenth [verses] of the fourth [stoma].

Or else, there are four *pṛṣṭhas* and eighteen [stotras] in the *parokṣa* manner. The fifth is the *ājya* of the Hotṛ, and the two subsequent *pavamānas* consist of eighteen [verses]. The *pṛṣṭha* of the Hotṛ is the *parikrī*, and the *bahiṣpavamāna* consists of twenty-four [verses]; those desiring heaven perform this sacrifice.
The *anukriyā* is the lowest and most inferior; its two subsequent *pavamāna* chants consist of twenty-four verses each.
The horse-attendant is the announcer of the Soma.
There is only one horseman; there is no chariot-rider. 6.
And Dadhīcī spoke thus at the end within the three sheaths.
The female cow is the one for purchasing the Soma. || 8 ||
The tip of the sacrificial post is sharpened. ||9||
The *saṃmīlana* rite, the altar (*vedi*), the two *havirdhāna* sheds, the *agnīṣomīya* animal sacrifice, the *vasatīvarī* waters, and the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*). ||17.2.10||
And here, the choosing of an enemy is the same as in the first case. || 11 ||
Whatever [he desires], by means of self-sovereignty, he immediately attains self-sovereignty. ||12||
By means of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice for Agni, one obtains all kinds of food. || 13 ||
The Agniṣṭoma with one hundred and three verses belongs to Prajāpati; he attains Prajāpati. || 14 ||
In the rite for the desire to overcome rivals, there is the immolation of an animal, a meal, gold, a garment, and the bringing forward of a bed; the *sadas* hall is the same as in the first [rite].
The Soma-proclaimer and the curd-skin bag. || 16 ||
In this case, the Aśvin-verse is supreme; in the middle, the officiating priests remain separated by a krośa. || 17 ||

Having approached him in the morning, [the sacrificer thinks]: "Prajāpati is the wheat; the field is the altar; the threshing floor of wheat is the high altar (uttaravedi); the two sheds for the oblation-materials are the mounting stairs; the measured hall is the Sadas; the wooden sword (sphya) is the sacrificial post, either with its tip intact or a threshing-pole (khalevālī). A white mare is the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā); it is to be given to the Brahman priest. The distribution of fees to the others is as in the archetype. Having announced his intention to his rival, he should sacrifice with the Caturviṃśastotrīya. By means of the Viśvajit sacrifice, characterized by all the Stomas, he attains all desires. || 18 ||
One who practices sorcery should sacrifice with the Śyena.
The two chariots are the two oblation-holders. || 17.2.20 ||
The sacrificial post (yūpa) is made of *tailvaka* or *bādhaka* wood and has a point like a wooden sword (*sphya*).
The two pressing-boards are made of Śāvana wood. || 22 ||
A red animal for Agni accompanied by Rudra. || 23 ||
He deposits the Upāṃśu and Antaryāma [cups].
The sacrificial grass is made of reeds. || 25 ||
The fuel is made of Vibhīdaka wood. || 26 ||
The officiating priests, wearing red turbans and red garments with their sacred threads suspended over the right shoulder, proceed with the ritual. || 27 ||
Their ears are ever-new and turned downward; they are deformed and crooked. || 28 ||
At the time of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), they should pierce it with thorns. || 29 ||

There are three Vācastomas; two of them are Agniṣṭomas. The Sarvastoma Atirātra is the last. In that [Atirātra], all the Ṛks, all the Sāmans, and all the Yajus formulas should be employed. || 17.2.30 ||
The Praghāsa and the Vrātyastomas belong to the Vrātyas. || 31 ||
The Agniṣṭoma is Trivṛt with the Rathantara Sāman; the Ukthyas have the Dviṣati Stomas; all [the Ukthyas] have the Ṣoḍaśin. || 32 ||

A turban, a goad, a bowstring, a foot-rest for the chariot, a carriage with uneven wheels, a chariot covered with wooden planks, a horse, a mule, two draft animals, a black garment, a black-and-white antelope skin, and a silver neck-ornament. || 33 ||
That belongs to the householder. || 34 ||
The fringes of the cords for others are made of wool. || 35 ||
Two cords and two sandals. || 36 ||
The skins of wild animals are joined in pairs. || 37 ||
Thirty-three [deities] approach each householder. || 38 ||
These are the sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās). || 39 ||
Alternatively, sixty-six cows constitute the sacrificial fee.
Moreover, they say that one should give whatever of theirs has been acquired; for it is known: "That indeed is the wealth of a Vrātya. ||41||
The six-ṣoḍaśin is for those who are censured; the two-ṣoḍaśin is for the youngest; the half-stoma is for the eldest; the four-ṣoḍaśin is for all.
The offering of the Ādityas is worthy of praise; he is the first among those who dwell in the firmament. || 43 ||
They attain freedom from evil and from their rival. || 44 ||

The other Agniṣṭomas are those of the Aṅgirases; the second is that of the Sādhyas; the third is that of the Maruts, by which one obtains vigor and heroism. Some say the thirty-third is the fifth; others say the fifth is that of Prajāpati. One who desires offspring [performs it]; he overcomes his rival, he overcomes (the rival). By means of its removal, he removes the rival. (Section 5) ||45||
The Citistoma sacrifice is for one desiring progeny. || 46 ||
A Brāhmaṇa desiring the office of domestic priest should sacrifice with the Gāyatra Ukthya and the Rathantara Sāman; for the Brāhmaṇa, the first two [stotras] are Gāyatra. 47.
The *uttara* [is] for the Kṣatriya. || 48 ||
Luster is the spiritual splendor of a Brahmin; it is in the east for him, while for a Kṣatriya it is in the north—fierce yet not causing distress—but neither of them possesses many cattle. ||49||
One who has not been purified should sacrifice with the Trivṛt Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma.
The *purorucaḥ* verses are dedicated to Agni; the *subrahmaṇyā* formula is dedicated to Agni. 51.
They chant the hymns for Agni; a goat and gold are the sacrificial fee. ||52||
Having performed this very Catuḥṣṭoma sacrifice, one who is learned in the Vedas (śrotriya)—whether struck by dice, struck by women, struck by lust, or struck by his own conduct—should perform it.
A dark-brown horse is the sacrificial fee. || 54 ||
That is to be given to a Brahmin. || 55 ||
As in the case of the original nature, so it is with others. || 56 ||

Having made the Vāyavyā verses the fifteen-fold Agniṣṭoma-sāman of this very sacrifice, one should cause one who is afflicted by disease to sacrifice; or one who desires food, or one who desires offspring, or one who desires cattle. 57.

Having made the Vāravantīya the Agniṣṭoma-sāman upon these very Revatī verses for one desiring spiritual luster; having made the Vāravantīya the Agniṣṭoma-sāman upon the Śakvarī verses for one desiring cattle; having performed this very same Catuḥṣṭoma for one desiring a village. (Some say they are without the Pravargya rite. One desiring spiritual luster [should perform] the Agniṣṭut with the Trivṛt stoma; one desiring vigor [should perform] the Agniṣṭut with the Pañcadaśa stoma. 58.
One who has failed in a sacrifice, or in whatever sacrificial rite he may have stumbled, should perform the seventeen-fold Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma.
One who speaks should speak with the *trivṛt* [chant]. 17.2.60.
The fifteenth [day] belongs to one who slays or causes another to be slain. || 61 ||

The seventeenth [chapter] concerns the eating of food that should not be eaten; having consumed it, one must wait twenty-one days before visiting people from Gāndhāra, Kaliṅga, Māgadha, Pāraskara, or Sauvīra.
One desiring vigor [should perform] the Triṇava [stoma]. || 63 ||

With the fifteenfold [stoma], one who desires vigor; with the seventeenfold, one who desires offspring; with the twenty-onefold, one who desires a firm foundation; (with the thirty-threefold, one who desires heaven). ||64||
Or rather, it is the Jyotiṣṭoma itself; in the Agniṣṭoma, one may desire all desires. (Section 6) 65.
Thus ends the second chapter in the seventeenth book of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi Sūtra.
Now begins the third chapter in the seventeenth book:
One desiring food should sacrifice with the Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, which is undefined (anirukta). 1.
Some say that the morning pressing is undefined.
A white horse is the sacrificial fee; it is to be given to the Brahman priest. 3.
The Bṛhaspatisava is the second [offering]. ||4||

A Brāhmaṇa who desires spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) or the office of domestic priest (*purodhā*), or one whom they might consecrate for the position of a ruler (*sthāpatya*), should perform this sacrifice. The Hotṛ priest wears a garland (*parisrajī*).
Aruṇa, Mirmira, and Triśukra. || 7 ||
With the verse, "O Bṛhaspati, be pleased with us," he draws the Atigrāhya cup dedicated to Bṛhaspati.
An animal sacred to Bṛhaspati is to be immolated. ||9||
At the morning pressing, when the Nārāśaṃsa cups have been set down, he assigns eleven sacrificial gifts.

At the midday pressing, he consecrates him with clarified butter while he is holding onto the fire on a black antelope skin; or as in the piling of the fire-altar, with the residue of the *śukra* and *manthin* cups.
At the midday pressing, he dedicates twelve horses; at both [pressings] together, he dedicates those [animals]; and at the third pressing, twelve [cattle].
He dedicates her as a barren cow. || 13 ||

Alternatively, there may be eight at the morning pressing, eleven at the midday pressing, and twelve at the third pressing. According to some, one should give a horse at each pressing in three parts; according to others, all [the gifts] at the midday pressing.
Neither in the two other *savana*s [forenoon and afternoon] by means of the mind, nor indeed by the mind alone.
Having performed the drawing of the arrow from the threefold Agniṣṭoma, one who practices sorcery should sacrifice.
The rest is the same as for the Śyena. || 17 ||
The Agniṣṭoma consists of the Trivṛt [stoma]. || 18 ||
The Śunaḥśepa-stoma; the Sarvasvāra. 19.
It is known from scripture: "He who desires death should sacrifice; he who desires freedom from disease and wishes to go to the heavenly world [should sacrifice]. (17.3.20)
A parrot-green animal is to be sacrificed to Yama. || 21 ||
The sacrificial fee consists of prepared food. || 22 ||

While the Ārbhava Pavamāna is being chanted, he wraps himself with a large cloth having its fringes pointing downward, covers himself with it from the right side, and lies down with his head toward the south, saying: "O Brāhmaṇas, complete this sacrifice! (Section 7). The sacrifice concludes following its formal conclusion. 23.

Having consigned the fires into separate fire-drills (*araṇī*) and having worshipped the sun with the *Uttaranārāyaṇa* hymn, he departs for the forest. If he should dwell in a village, he should consign the fires into separate fire-drills, worship the sun with the *Uttaranārāyaṇa*, and settle back in his home. Regarding those sacrificial rites (*yajñakratu*) that he might not reach, [the scripture] says: "The *Bhūrukthya* sacrifice, having the *Rathantara* as its *Sāman*, one desiring prosperity should perform; a cow is the sacrificial fee. (24)
Indeed, the merit of one who performs the Cāturmāsya sacrifices is truly inexhaustible.
The Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma is in the world of the Vaiśvadevas. || 26 ||
The sacrificial animal belongs to the Viśvedevas; the animal to be bound after the Soma sacrifice belongs to Bṛhaspati.
They do not erect a sacrificial post. || 28 ||
They do not throw up the northern altar. || 29 ||

They tie the animal to the enclosing-stick, or to a firebrand, or to the sacrificial grass. They erect the [other] posts in the northern part; they scatter earth around the northern altar. || 17.3.30 ||

Then, after four months, in the world of the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings, there is a three-night sacrifice consisting of an Agniṣṭoma, an Ukthya, and an Atirātra. There is an animal sacrifice for the Maruts, a second one for Varuṇa, and a Maitrāvaruṇī Anūbandhyā cow as the concluding offering.
Then, after four months, in the world of the Sākamedhas, there is a three-night sacrifice consisting of an Agniṣṭoma, an Ukthya, and an Atirātra.
The animal for Agni is first; the one for Indra and Agni is second; those of the eleven-day set are third, or else the one dedicated to Prajāpati, followed by the Saura *anūbandhya* sacrifice.

Then, after four months, there is the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice with the Catuṣṭoma stoma at the Śunāsīrīya festival; the animal victim is dedicated to Vāyu, and the Anūbandhyā cow is dedicated to the Aśvins.

Wearing a garment that has not been washed, having emerged from the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*), during the intervals between sacrifices he does not speak untruth, does not eat meat, does not approach a woman, and does not sit on elevated ground. He should detest falsehood; he sleeps facing the east; he does not eat honey; he does not apply collyrium to his eyes, nor does he anoint himself with oil. He may approach his wife only during her season (*ṛtu*). (Section 8) 35.
Thus ends the third chapter in the seventeenth book of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-Sūtra.
Now begins the fourth chapter in the seventeenth book.

There are fifty sacrificial fees for the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice; one hundred for the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices; one hundred and fifty for the Sākamedha sacrifices; and twelve hundred for the Śunāsīrīya sacrifice. 1.
Or they may be offered according to the season, or according to their respective [deities] during the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.
At the third pressing, he should release the calves together with their mothers. || 3 ||

One should cause a person suffering from illness to sacrifice with the Upahavya Agniṣṭoma, using either the Rathantara-sāman, the Bṛhat-sāman, or both sāmans. With this same sacrifice, one should cause a person desiring food, desiring offspring, or desiring cattle to sacrifice. A dark-grey horse is the sacrificial fee; it is to be given to the Brahman priest.
As in the case of the original nature, so it is with the others. ||5||
A Brāhmaṇa desiring all objects of desire should perform the Ṛtuprayenāgniṣṭoma with the Bṛhat Sāman. ||6||
There are six initiations (dīkṣās) and six preparatory days (upasads). He observes the vow of clarified butter (ghṛtavrata). || 7 ||
As long as this first stalk of grain [is not yet offered], so long is the vow maintained when the Soma has been purchased.
By means of the subsequent Uttara-kāṇḍa, he enters upon the vow.
At night he sits facing the fire; by day, facing the sun.
Having uttered the *ṛta*, they move forward; speaking the *ṛta*, they consume [the offering]. 11.
A four-cornered ladle made of udumbara wood, filled with soma, should be given to a dear kinsman who is a Brahmin. || 12 ||
As in the case of the original nature, so it is with others. || 13 ||
By means of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice performed with abundant gold, one attains the world of oxen; one conquers the luminous worlds. || 14 ||
At the consecration ceremony (dīkṣaṇīyā), he gives gold weighing twelve mānas; at the introductory ceremony (prāyaṇīyā), twice that amount.

Thus, from this point upward, by doubling [the number of repetitions] at each stage—at the Ātithyā, at the Upasads, at the Pravargyas, when the omentum of the Agniṣomīya animal has been offered, at the Agniṣomīya, when the omentum of the Savanīya animal has been offered, and at the Savanīya during the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana). ||16||

When the Nārāśaṃsa cups have been consumed, at the Avabhṛtha sacrifice, at the Udayanīya offering, when the omentum of the Anūbandhyā cow has been offered, at the Anūbandhyā itself, and finally at the Udavasānīya. (Section 9) 17.
A Brāhmaṇa desiring spiritual luster should perform the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, which is threefold, characterized by the Agniṣṭut, and accompanied by the Rathantara Sāman. || 18 ||

With the fifteen-fold Indrastuta Ukthya sacrifice, characterized by the Bṛhat Sāman, a Rājanya desiring heroism [should sacrifice]. With the seventeen-fold Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, characterized by the Kaṇvarathantara Sāman, a Vaiśya desiring the prosperity of cattle [should sacrifice].
At the morning pressing, he mixes all the Soma juices with curds; at the midday pressing, with boiled milk; and at the third pressing, with curds. ||21||
Or with that which is mixed with what has been brought [from elsewhere]. || 22 ||
One should cause a Soma-vomiter to sacrifice with the Tīvrasut, the Ukthya, the Rathantara-sāman, the Bṛhat-sāman, or the Ubhayasāman. || 23 ||

One should cause a king who has been overthrown, who desires a village, who desires offspring, who desires cattle, or who has fallen away from prosperity, to sacrifice with the Somātipavita; one should sacrifice it when practicing sorcery against another, or when being subjected to sorcery oneself. 24.
At the morning pressing, he mixes all the Soma juices with curds; at the midday pressing, with boiled milk; at the third pressing, with curds, or with the mixture of boiled milk and curds.
They milk the boiled [milk] into the āśir mixture. || 26 ||
They milk the cow that has recently calved, using the milk of another calf for the āśira mixture. || 27 ||
These are the sacrificial gifts (dakṣiṇās). || 28 ||
They pour out [the Soma] into the additional cups. || 29 ||
The officiating priests smell [the portions] but do not eat them. || 17.4.30 ||
They consume them during the chant of the Acchāvāka. || 31 ||
The Hotrakas seek an invitation from the Brahman priest. || 32 ||
Both the sacrificer and the officiating priests—the two Adhvaryus and all the Camasādhvaryus—respond to the Acchāvāka. || 33 ||
The first set of eleven is combined.
They dig up the altar as far as the sacrificial post. || 35 ||
A white mare is the sacrificial fee; it is to be given to the Brahman priest. || 36 ||
As in the case of the original nature, so it is with the others. || 37 ||
Through the Marutstoma sacrifice, the king and the royal priest attain union [with the deity]. || 38 ||
Now, this is the Rāṭ sacrifice. He who, desiring a kingdom, does not obtain it, should perform this sacrifice. (Section 10) || 39 ||
Thus ends the fourth paṭala in the seventeenth praśna of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-sūtra.

Now begins the fifth paṭala in the seventeenth [praśna]. One desiring food should perform the Virāj sacrifice; one desiring stability—or, according to some, offspring—should perform the Svarāj sacrifice. ||1||

He who, having accepted much [gifts], should feel as if he has swallowed poison, or having eaten food that should not be eaten, or, according to some, having officiated at a sacrifice for one for whom one should not officiate—he should perform this *punarstoma*. He who is light-minded and lacks a firm foundation should perform it with the twenty-one-fold *stoma* and the *aupacchada* chant. According to some, one desiring offspring should perform it with the twenty-one-fold *stoma* and the *aupacchada* chant.
One who desires a firm foundation [should perform] the *aupacchedana* [offering]. ||2||
One chants along with each individual *stotriyā* verse. || 3 ||
At the morning pressing, he scatters dust beneath the *pūtabhṛt* vessel with the formula: "May the Gandharvas and Apsarases rejoice. || 4 ||
"May the Gandharvas and the gods rejoice," [he says] at the midday pressing; "May the Gandharvas and the ancestors rejoice," [he says] at the third pressing. (5)
They say, "Flee! ||6||
Furthermore, having accepted much through a sacrifice, one who might feel as if he has swallowed poison while being falsely accused—let him become one of these [vows].
One who desires cattle [should sacrifice] with the two Gotama-catuṣṭomas. || 8 ||
The subsequent [sacrifice] consists of the Ukthya and the Ṣoḍaśin. || 9 ||
You two are like neuter sacrificial animals. || 17.5.10 ||
One who desires cattle [should sacrifice] with the Udbhid and Balabhid [sacrifices]. || 11 ||
Having caused [the ground] to be excavated, one should sacrifice with the Balabhid [offering] after a year has passed.
One enters the intermediate space with a cake on eight potsherds dedicated to Agni. || 13 ||
In both cases, he gives the Gāyatrīs in their entirety as the sacrificial fee. || 14 ||
There are eight in the east and eight in the north.
One who desires honor [should worship] with the two verses beginning with "apaciti. || 16 ||
Both possess the same characteristics. || 17 ||
With two birds that have piled altars, [one should sacrifice] for him who should desire: "May I move along the luminous heavenly worlds like a bird. ||18||
One should cause a kṣatriya who desires heroism to sacrifice with the Ṛṣabha-agniṣṭoma. || 19 ||
A bull is the sacrificial fee. || 17.5.20 ||
One who desires self-sovereignty should perform the Gosava sacrifice with the Ukthya rite, using the Bṛhat and Rathantara Sāmans. || 21 ||
The sacrificial fee is ten thousand. ||22||

To the south of the Āhavanīya fire, while the altar has not yet been leveled, he is consecrated with the Māhendra-stotra at the time of the *pratidhuṣa*. "Born wealthy, increased by power, the best among the lords of lords, the bestower of vital strength; great, established in greatness, be watchful over the lordly power and the kingdom! With the self-sovereignty of Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin, I consecrate thee! (23)
Having performed the Gosava sacrifice, he observes the cow-vow for one year or for twelve days.
He approaches as if toward his mother, his sister, or a woman of the same lineage; he drinks water or cuts grass as if it were near him. || 25 ||
Wherever excrement might find him, there he stands, having plunged into it like a cow; thus have I suffered. || 26 ||
Through the hymn of praise to the Maruts, one nourishes immeasurable prosperity. || 27 ||
With this [rite], one should cause three [persons] to sacrifice. || 28 ||
With the Indrastoma, the Ukthya, the Rathantara-sāman, the Bṛhat-sāman, or the Ubhaya-sāman—by means of that, he should cause two [sacrificers] to sacrifice. ||29||
By means of the Ṛṣabha sacrifice, the Agniṣṭoma with the Bṛhat-sāman, a Brāhmaṇa becomes the sovereign of his equals. || 17.5.30 ||
One should have both the king and the domestic priest perform a sacrifice together in a single ritual using the *kulāya* of Indra and Agni. || 31 ||
He enters the people as their king in order to fully secure splendor and the luster of sacred knowledge. || 32 ||
By striking down the enemy who is free from sin with the *vidhanana* [chant], all adversaries are struck down by it. || 33 ||
One who has rivals [should sacrifice] with the *saṃdaṃśa* cup; one practicing sorcery, with the *vajra* and the *ṣoḍaśin*; this has been explained by [the rules for] the *śyena*. || 34 ||
One desiring increase [of life] should perform the Trayodaśarātra and the Trirātra rites. || 35 ||
One who desires prosperity should perform the Sarvastoma sacrifice. || 36 ||
One who desires cattle should perform the Aptoryāma sacrifice. || 37 ||
For [he thinks], "Lest the animals should fall away. || 38 ||
The sacrificial animals consist of groups of eleven. || 39 ||
One desiring offspring [should sacrifice] with a seventeenfold [stoma]. || 17.5.40 ||
By means of the Viṣuvat day, one who is the eldest son of the eldest wife attains preeminence.
One who has rivals should perform the Goṣṭoma sacrifice. || 42 ||
One who desires heaven [should perform it] for the sake of long life. || 43 ||
One who desires cattle should perform [the sacrifice] with the Abhijit [constellation]. || 44 ||
One who desires a village should perform the Viśvajit sacrifice. || 45 ||
One who desires spiritual luster [should perform the sacrifice] with *trivṛt* [bricks]. || 46 ||
With the fifteenth [day], one who desires vigor [should sacrifice]. || 47 ||
One desiring offspring should [sacrifice] with the seventeenfold [stoma]. || 48 ||
One desiring a firm foundation [should sacrifice] with the twenty-first [stotra]. (kha012) || 49 ||
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the seventeenth book of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi Sūtra.
Now begins the sixth chapter in the seventeenth book:
"The Ahīna sacrifices, beginning with the Dvirātra and ending with the Ekādaśarātra, are those that have an Atirātra at the end. (1)
By means of their twelve-day Ahīna sacrifice, the Kalpa is explained. || 2 ||
For the two-night, three-night, four-night, five-night, seven-night, or nine-night sacrifice, the first draught is that for Indra and Vāyu; or it may be that for Śukra.
On the second day of the two-night rite, he draws the Ṣoḍaśin cup.
In the middle [of the series], starting from the three-night [sacrifice] and the four-night [sacrifice] and so forth among the various *ahīna* sacrifices. || 5 ||
He who is meritorious like an Ahīna sacrifice should perform this sacrifice with the Āṅgirasa [Sāman].
For him, the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma constitutes the first day.
The Sarvastoma Atiratra is the subsequent [sacrifice]. || 8 ||
On the first day, the Gāyatra is the Sāman; on the following day, the Traiṣṭubha. ||9||
On the first day, the Rathantara becomes the Sāman.
In the Bṛhaduttara [Sāman], verse 11.
On the preceding day, the Vaikhānasa Sāman is performed; on the following day, the Ṣoḍaśin.
The first day has *haviṣmat* as its *nidhana*; the subsequent [day] has *haviṣkṛt* as its *nidhana*. 13.
On the new moon day, the first day is for sacrificing; the following day is for the subsequent sacrifice.
Whatever desire one may desire by means of the Kāpivana [Sāman], that one attains through this. || 15 ||
For him, the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma constitutes the first day; the Atirātra is the latter.
By means of the Caitraratha [sāman], one secures all kinds of food. ||17||
For him, the first day is an Agniṣṭoma with the Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa stomas, and the next day is an Atirātra.
By means of the Garga-trirātra sacrifice, one ascends to the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas. || 19 ||
He becomes firmly established in these worlds. ||17.6.20||
The Agniṣṭoma, the Ukthya, and the Atirātra are the three days; the Rathantara, Vāmadevya, and Bṛhat are the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.
There is a cake on eleven potsherds for Agni and Viṣṇu, an oblation of cooked rice for Sarasvatī, and an oblation of cooked rice for Bṛhaspati;
or [he may perform] the Dīkṣaṇīyā or the Traidhātavīyā offering. (Section 13) 22.
The Soma-purchasing cow is tawny, reddish-brown, ruddy, with reddish-brown eyes, and one year old. || 23 ||

A thousand is the sacrificial fee for the first day; one should lead three hundred on the second (and third), and thirty-three likewise; thus the thousand is exceeded. The two forms of the Rohiṇī are both reddish-brown, or reddish-brown on one side.
One should lead her on the first day, or on the last day, if she is the most excellent.

On the first day, he should give [the horse] with the mantra: "O Agni, you have brought us a thousandfold strength; you have destroyed [our enemies]. Bring us a thousandfold [blessing] together with progeny and cattle; may wealth enter me again. He consecrates that [horse] as it is being led out with the mantra: "A stallion in the second [birth], you have become full of sap through the sap of the waters and the plants."

"May she endow me with a thousandfold, together with offspring and cattle; may wealth come back to me again"—with these words [he addresses] a barren cow or a dwarf bull at the third [offering]. "Thou art the support of a thousand, thou art the dwarf belonging to Viṣṇu. Bestow upon us a thousandfold, together with offspring and cattle; may wealth come back to me again. || 26 ||
He releases that dwarf [image] toward the east, as many as a thousand times. || 27 ||
If they were to bestow one boon each upon him, he would be born again as a performer of a thousand sacrifices to the Sun. || 28 ||
Having led it around the north of the Āgnīdhra fire, he should cause it to smell the Droṇakalaśa at the edge of the Āhavanīya fire. || 29 ||

Having led [the Soma] either to the south of the altar or between the sacrificial post and the Āhavanīya fire, or between the Āgnīdhra shed and the Havirdhāna shed, he should cause [the sacrificer] to smell the Droṇakalaśa with the formula, "Smell the jar. (17.6.30)

Having brought [the garment] to the Āgnīdhra fire-shed from the north, and having placed a *tārpya* (linen cloth) upon it, while it stands facing west in front [of him], he offers an oblation in the Āgnīdhra shed with the verse, "Both of you have conquered. Upon that *tārpya*, the form of the *adhiṣṇiya* hearths is knotted. || 31 ||
Having led her toward the western corner of the Sadas with the words, "They have eaten the Iḍā," he murmurs [the following] at her right ear.

If he abandons it and attains consciousness while it has been carried away by a non-human being toward the east, one should know: "This sacrificer has won a beautiful world. If it is toward the south, one should know: "He will depart quickly from this world. If it is toward the west, one should know: "He will possess abundant grain. If it is toward the north, one should know: "He will become superior in this world. || 33 ||
One should give it to the Āgnīdhra, or to the Brahman, or to the Hotṛ, or to the Adhvaryu. || 34 ||

Or he may appoint two Udgātṛs; he should give [the fee] to whichever of them does not call for the *āśrāvaṇa*. Or he should give two [shares] to the Brahman on the third occasion, and the third to the Agnīdh.

"May she lead me to the heavenly world; may she lead me to the luminous world; may she lead me to all the worlds of merit; may she lead me to a firm foundation together with offspring and cattle; may wealth return to me again"—having consecrated [the gift] with this mantra, he gives it. Thus it is said. 36.

He should accept it with the formula: "Thou art one, not a thousand; I accept thee as one being, not as a thousand. Enter me as one, do not enter me as a thousand. Thou art pleasant, easy to sit upon, and very gracious; enter me pleasantly, enter me easily to sit upon, enter me very graciously. ||37||
Having ransomed that [cow] with another cow, he releases it into the pens of the sacrificer's cattle. || 38 ||
Having brought together those thirty-three [cows] that were in excess, they milk ten for the first day, twenty for the second, and thirty for the third.
On the first day, prepared food should be given; on the second, gold, a cow, or clothing; and on the third, a cart, a chariot, a horse, an elephant, or a man. || 17.6.40 ||

One who possesses a lineage of seers (*ārṣeya*) and is learned should be given [the gift] on the first day; one who lacks a lineage of seers but is learned, on the second; and one who possesses a lineage of seers but is unlearned, on the third. || 41 ||

When leading the sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), one should lead them in groups of ten; for whomsoever one intends to give a single cow, one should add it to a group of thirteen; for whomsoever five, [one adds it] to those ten; for whomsoever three, [one adds it] to those ten; for whomsoever one, [one adds it] to a single [group]; for whomsoever five, [one adds it] to two [groups] to make a ten; thus, up to a hundred or even a thousand, one should give something, saying "a thousand."

If he should give [the gift], he should give it when the omentum of the Anūbandhyā cow has been offered; or he should give it at the Udavasānīyā sacrifice, having sacrificed the final oblation, led away the highest sacrificial fee, and either departed or remained.

"O Śabalī, you are the ocean; you are all-pervading. You are the Brahman, the first-born of the gods. You are the food of the cosmic order (ṛta); you are the pure, you are the light, you are the splendor, you are the immortal. We know you, O Śabalī, as the radiant one. Of you, the earth is one foot, the intermediate space is one foot, the sky is one foot, the ocean is one foot; the world beyond the dust (parorajas) is your fifth foot. You are this Śabalī; milk for us nourishment and vigor, the stream of wealth. O Śabalī, having been born, may I enter the vow of the glorious ones. Svāhā!"—with these words he offers the Śabalī oblation. ||44||
(The invocation of the Subrahmaṇyā priest:
It is either obligatory or optional. (Section 15) || 45 ||
Thus ends the sixth chapter in the seventeenth book of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-Sūtra.
Now, the seventh chapter in the seventeenth book:
He who, desiring a kingdom, does not obtain it by means of the *Vaida-trirātra* sacrifice, should perform this [sacrifice].

It consists of three *atirātra* sacrifices, each with three rounds (*trivṛt*), all of them featuring the *ṣoḍaśin* cup; the *pṛṣṭha* stotras are the *rathantara*, the *vāmadevya*, and the *bṛhat*. By means of the Garga-trirātra, the days of the subsequent three [sacrifices] are explained.
One who desires cattle [should perform] the Chandoma Pavamāna sacrifice. || 3 ||
He obtains cattle that contain wealth within them. ||4||
One who desires heaven [should perform] the Parāka penance. || 5 ||
Atreḥ [sacrifice] is twenty-fourfold; it is a four-night rite. Four heroes are born from him: a good Hotṛ, a good Udgātṛ, a good Adhvaryu, and one who is successful in the assembly. || 6 ||
The Agniṣṭoma is the first day.
The Ukthya is the middle [day] and the Atirātra follows; the Pavamāna-stotras consist of the twenty-four-fold stoma, and thus the days of the other three [sacrificial sessions] are explained. || 8 ||
By the son of Jamadagni; they nourish their former prosperities. 9.

The Upasad days involve offerings of sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*). There is a cake on one potsherd for Agni; a cake on two potsherds for the Aśvins; a cake on three potsherds for Viṣṇu; a cake on four potsherds for Soma; a cake on five potsherds for Savitṛ; a cake on six potsherds for Dhātṛ; a cake on seven potsherds for the Maruts; a cake on eight potsherds for Bṛhaspati; a cake on nine potsherds for Mitra; a cake on ten potsherds for Varuṇa; a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra; and a cake on twelve potsherds for the Viśvedevas. (Section 16) There are also oblations offered with the *darvi*-ladle (*darvihoma*).

O Agni, perform the office of the Hotṛ; perform the sacrifice. Bring hither Vaiśvānara, the Father, for our protection. For Indra and for the gods, may the oblation be pleasing; Svāhā! O divine Aśvins, with the honeyed stalk, sprinkle the sacrifice today for the sacrificer. O divine Viṣṇu, stride through this sacrifice today for the sacrificer. O divine Soma, bestower of seed, be present today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer. O divine Savitṛ, well-impelled, impel everything favorably today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer.

O divine Dhātar, O Sudhātar, be present today at this sacrifice for the sake of the sacrificer. O divine pressing-stones, speak honeyed speech today at this sacrifice for the sake of the sacrificer. O divine Aditi, favor this sacrifice today for the sake of the sacrificer. O divine Aditi, being well-disposed toward the Ādityas, press out the Soma today at this sacrifice for the sake of the sacrificer. O divine Anumati, approve this sacrifice today for the sake of the sacrificer. O divine Waters, bow down here today at this sacrifice for the sake of the sacrificer.

"Seat by seat, O Prajāpati, bestowing men, being pleased, O Indra, lord of gods, as the possessor of power, be present today at this sacrifice for the sake of the sacrificer! O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, bestower of good seed, be present today at this sacrifice for the sake of the sacrificer! Having thus recited these responses, the oblations are made. To every one of them he adds the formula: "May the oblation be pleasing to Indra and the gods; Svāhā! (17.7.10)
The Saṃsarpa belongs to Vasiṣṭha; he who is virtuous as if he were an Ahīna sacrifice should perform this sacrifice.
One who has rivals should perform the sacrifice of Viśvāmitra Saṃjaya. (Khaṇḍa 17) 12.
By means of five days of the year, he is indeed born. || 13 ||
He obtains a thousand cattle. || 14 ||
He becomes a speaker of words. || 15 ||
The Agniṣṭoma is Trivṛt; the Ukthya is Pañcadaśa; the Ukthya is Saptadaśa; and the Agniṣṭoma is Pañcaviṃśa, accompanied by the Mahāvrata. || 16 ||
The Viśvajit is an Atirātra sacrifice characterized by all the Pṛṣṭha-stotras.
By means of repeated practice. ||18||

Whatever desire one desires, that he attains through the Agniṣṭoma, the three Ukthyas, and the Atirātra. Two pressings are of the Trivṛt stoma; one pressing is of the Pañcadaśa; two pressings are of the Pañcadaśa; one pressing is of the Saptadaśa; two pressings are of the Saptadaśa; one pressing is of the Ekaviṃśa; two pressings are of the Ekaviṃśa; one pressing is of the Triṇava; two pressings are of the Triṇava; and one [pressing] is of the Trayastriṃśa. || 19 ||
By means of the Pañcaśāradīya sacrifice, one becomes greater than great. || 17.7.20 ||
One should sacrifice with the animal sacrifice (paśubandha) every year. || 21 ||
They bring seventeen speckled oxen five years old, and seventeen speckled heifers three years old that have not yet calved. || 22 ||
They immolate the other animals that have been sprinkled and carried around the fire. || 23 ||
They do not release the others. || 24 ||
Then, after a year, they bring reddish cows with speckled butter-like markings and other bulls; having sprinkled them and carried fire around them, they immolate the others and release the rest.

Then, after a year, they bring tawny and dappled cows. They immolate those bulls that have been sprinkled with water and carried around the fire, while they release the others. After a year, they bring lotus-colored cows. They immolate those bulls that have been sprinkled with water and carried around the fire, while they release the others. (Khaṇḍa 18) 27.

In the fifth year, there are Soma sacrifices: a *trivṛt* *agniṣṭoma*, a *pañcadaśa* *ukthya*, a *saptadaśa* *ukthya*, a *pañcadaśa* *agniṣṭoma*, and a *saptadaśa* *atirātra*. One should complete the departure on the preceding full moon day; these bulls become the *savanīya* victims. A goat is for Agni-Soma; every day he immolates three each. In the same way, following this, there are bulls for Indra-Maruts and heifers for the Maruts. 28.

If Rudra should strike the bull, one should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni accompanied by Rudra and then dedicate another victim. If it should die in water, [one should offer] a pap to Apām Napāt. If it should sink, a pap to Nirṛti. If it should break a limb, a cake on one potsherd to Bhūmi. If it should fall into a pit, a cake on three potsherds to Viṣṇu. If it should be lame or humpbacked, a pap to Bṛhaspati. If it should be blind or one-eyed, a cake on one potsherd to Sūrya.

If they should carry him off by force, he should offer a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Prasaha. If he should find a female wolf in the army or a tiger should kill him, he should sacrifice a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra. If he should perish [in battle], he should offer a pap to Vāyu. If he should die by this [natural] death, he should offer a cake on twelve potsherds to Prajāpati.
At the Mahāvrata, there is the Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma; the Gaur Ukthya, the Mahāvrata, the Gaur Ukthya, and the Āyu Atirātra. (Section 19) || 17.7.30 ||
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the seventeenth book of the *Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi-Sūtra*.
Now, in the context of the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*), he introduces the *sarvatomukha* (all-facing) rite:

"He who desires, 'May I become all this,' [should perform] the *sarvatomukha*. The *gārhapatya* fire is in the center. The sacrificial enclosures (*vihāra*) for the Soma rites are in each direction. In the eastern direction is the *trivṛt* [stoma]; in the south, the *pañcadaśa*; in the west, the *saptadaśa*; and in the north, the *ekaviṃśa*.
Now begins the eighth chapter in the seventeenth book:
One desiring heaven [should perform] the six-day rite for the Sādhyas.
The Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha. || 2 ||
They proceed with the Bṛhat and Rathantara [Sāmans]. ||3||
The Havirdhāna and the Āgnīdhra sheds are made of Aśvattha wood. || 4 ||
May you both possess wheels. || 5 ||
The sacrificial post has a mortar-base. || 6 ||
They go forward. ||7||
They go along the Sarasvatī; they go while shouting abuse. || 8 ||
When they perform a thousand [repetitions], then it is a single rising. || 9 ||
When they perform a hundred or a thousand [repetitions], then it is a single rising.
If one of them should die, or if they should be defeated, then there is a single rising.
One who desires heaven [should perform] the six-day rite of the seasons. || 12 ||
The *pṛṣṭhya* [six-day rite] is performed with the six-day period.
Above the gods, by means of the *trikadruka* [stotra], he attains a full lifespan and becomes more prosperous. || 14 ||

The Agniṣṭoma is Trivṛt, the Ukthya is Pañcadaśa, the Ukthya is Saptadaśa, and the Atirātra is Āyurgaujyotis. By means of this sacrifice, which is equal to a Sattra, one obtains food, progeny, cattle, vigor, and heroism. It consists of an Abhyāsaṅgya five-day period and a Viśvajit Atirātra. || 15 ||

With the Kausurubinda sacrifice lasting seven nights, one obtains cattle; it consists of five *pṛṣṭha* days, a twenty-five-fold *agniṣṭoma* with the Mahāvrata, and a *viśvajit* *atirātra* with all *pṛṣṭha* stotras. || 16 ||
One who desires the supernatural power of the Seven Sages. || 17 ||
The Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, the Trayastriṃśa, and the Mahāvrata [are performed] at the Atirātra.
The third [offering] belongs to Prajāpati, intended for one desiring progeny. || 19 ||
The Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, the Prājāpatya, the Trayastriṃśa, the Mahāvrata, and the Atirātra.

One who desires a firm foundation [should perform] with the support of the *pṛṣṭhya*; the *pṛṣṭhya* is a six-day period, the *pṛṣṭhya* is the support, the thirty-three-fold [stoma] is the *mahāvrata*, and the *atirātra* [concludes it]. 21.
One who desires cattle [should perform] the Chandomapavamāna; the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, the Chandomapavamāna, the Mahāvrata, and the Atirātra. (Section 20) 22.
Janaka, desiring a son, [performed this] for seven nights. || 23 ||

For that [sacrifice], there are four days consisting of the *trivṛt* stoma, beginning with the *agniṣṭoma*; the *viśvajit* and the *mahāvrata* are *atirātras*. By means of the seven-night rite dedicated to Indra (*aindra-saptarātra*), one surpasses other offspring; he becomes most powerful. There is a *trivṛt* *agniṣṭoma*, a *pañcadaśa* *ukthya*, a *saptadaśa* *ukthya*, an *abhijit* *agniṣṭoma*, and an *atirātra* containing all the *stomas*. || 24 ||

One desiring spiritual luster (brahmavarcasa) [should perform] the eight-night sacrifice: a *pṛṣṭhya* six-day period, a *pañcaviṃśa* *agniṣṭoma* accompanied by the *mahāvrata*, and a *sarvapṛṣṭha* *viśvajit* *atirātra*. || 25 ||
One who desires long life should sacrifice with three nine-night rites.
The Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, the Gauḥ and Āyus days, two *ahar*s, and the Viśvajit Atirātra. || 27 ||
With the second [set], one who desires spiritual luster should perform the Jyotis, Go, and Āyus three-day periods, the Abhyāsaṅgya five-day period, and the Viśvajit Atirātra. || 28 ||

With the *śalalī* and the tawny [bull]. Whatever desire one may desire, that he attains. The *jyotis*, the *go*, and the *āyuḥ* [form] three days; the *jyotis*, the *go*, and the *āyuḥ* [form] three days; the *āyuḥ*, the *go*, and the *āyuḥ* [form] the *atirātra*. (Section 21) 29.
There are four ten-night periods. || 17.8.30 ||
One who is about to undergo initiation for the ten-night sacrifice offers the Daśahotṛ oblation. || 31 ||
The *Indrasya Trikakud* ten-night sacrifice belongs to Indra; he who desires, "May I be like the three-peaked mountain among my peers," should perform this sacrifice. || 32 ||

The Agniṣṭut is an Agniṣṭoma with the Trivṛt stoma; the Ukthya has the Pañcadaśa stoma; the Agniṣṭoma has the Trivṛt stoma; the Ukthya has the Saptadaśa stoma; the Agniṣṭoma has the Saptadaśa stoma; the Agniṣṭoma has the Triṇava stoma; the Ukthya has the Trayastriṃśa stoma; the Agniṣṭoma has the Triṇava stoma; and the Viśvajit is an Atirātra with all the Pṛṣṭha-stotras. || 33 ||

Previously, one who is being subjected to malevolent magic (abhicāra) should sacrifice: a Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Jyotis Agniṣṭoma, a Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Jyotis Ukthya, a Gau Ukthya, an Āyus Ukthya, an Abhijit Agniṣṭoma, a Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, a Sarvajit Agniṣṭoma, and a Sarvastoma Atirātra. ||34||
